children.text: ) sma yudhiṣṭhiranakulasahadevabhīmasenārjunakauravādibhiḥ / anye rājānaḥ śabdamanuśrutaṃ śrutvā samāśvāsya svasthakāyā vyavasthitāḥ / sa ca tānevamāha - jīvanto yuṣmākamathavā mṛtāḥ? te kathayanti - jīvāmo bhagavan / tena mahāvīryeṇa puruṣeṇa sarvāṇi tāni dvārāṇi bhagnāni / yāvattāmraguhāyāṃ paśyati, sarve te rājāno bandhanabaddhāḥ / dṛṣṭvā ca nārāyaṇaṃ sarve te parasparaṃ vicintayanti - atha balirasurendro mṛtaḥ kālagataḥ? athavā punarapi maraṇakālo 'smākaṃ bhūtaḥ? atha te kathayanti - varamasmākaṃ saṃgrāmabhūmīmaraṇaṃ na tu bandhanabaddhānāṃ maraṇam / yadā bandhanabaddhāḥ kālaṃ kuryāma, tadā kṣatriyadharmamasmākaṃ vinaśyati / yadā saṃgrāmabhūmau kālaṃ kuryāma, tadā svargopagā vayaṃ bhavema //
children.translated_text: calling out to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Nakula</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, the <s>Kauravas</s>, and others. The other kings, hearing the sound, took heart and stood firm with restored bodies. And he spoke to them thus: "Are you alive or dead?" They replied: "We are alive, Blessed One!" By that man of great valor, all those gates were broken open. When he looked into the copper cave, all those kings were bound in chains. And upon seeing <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, all those kings reflected among themselves: "Has <s>Bali</s>, the lord of <s>asuras</s>, died and passed away? Or has the time of death come upon us again?" Then they said: "Better for us is death on the battlefield than death while bound in chains. If we were to die while bound in chains, then the <s>kṣatriya</s>-<s>dharma</s> (warrior's code) would perish for us. If we were to die on the battlefield, then we would become those who ascend to heaven."

Then the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, having gone there seeking an opportunity to descend, uprooted the seven mountains that had been placed at the gates. Having uprooted them, he easily hurled them to another place and proclaimed in a loud voice to those <s>kṣatriyas</s>,

children.text: atha te rājānaḥ sarve svakaṃ svakaṃ gṛhaṃ gatāḥ / tadā rathayogyānyaśvāni svakasvakāni sajjīkṛtāni / yadā te rathaṃ sajjīkurvanti mahārhāṇi śastrāṇi, tadā daśarathaputreṇa vāmanakarūpamabhinirmāya mṛgājinenottarya veṇudaṇḍamupagṛhya pīṭhikāmupagṛhya saṃprasthito matsakāśam / dvāramāgataḥ / dvārapālairanubaddhaḥ - mā praviśa vāmanaka brāhmaṇa iti / sa kathayati - dūrādevāhamāgataḥ / atha sa dvārapālastametadavocat - brāhmaṇa / katamasyā bhūmestvamāgataḥ? sa tamāhacandradvīpādrājarṣirahamāgataḥ / atha sa dvārapālapuruṣo gatvā balimārocayati - deva, āgataste vāmanako brāhmaṇaḥ / atha sa balistametadavocat - kīdṛśaṃ vastu yācate? atha sa dvārapālastametadavocat - deva na tamanujānāmi / atha sa balistametadavocat - gacchantu bhavantaḥ, ānīyatāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ / sa tairdvārapālapuruṣairāhūyoktaḥ - praviśa mahābrāhmaṇa / sa praviṣṭaḥ, ratnapīṭhamanupradattam / śukrastatraiva vyavasthitaḥ / sa ca tasyopādhyāya iti khyāyate / sa taṃ balimetadavocat - eṣa kālapuruṣo 'vapraviṣṭaḥ, avaśyaṃ te vighāto bhaviṣyati / balistametadavocat - kathaṃ jānāsi bhagavan? śukra uvāca - jānāmyahaṃ tasya nimittāni cihnāni ca dṛṣṭvā / balirāha - kimupāyaṃ vayaṃ kuryāmaḥ? atha nārāyaṇena vicintya avaśyaṃ dānasya vipratisāraṃ bhaviṣyati / tena me sarasvatī mukhe nyastā, tadā sa kathayati - āgaccha brāhmaṇa / kīdṛśamabhiprāyo bhavataḥ? sa praviśyaitadavocat - dvipadabhūmī yācayāmi / baliruvāca - yadi tvaṃ brāhmaṇa dvipadaṃ yācase, mayā trīṇi padāni te 'nupradattāni / sa pratigrahaṃ tasyopagṛhya svastimupavadyānugṛhītaṃ tena tilapānīyasuvarṇasahitam / tatastena vāmanakarūpamantardhāpitam / atha śukro balimetadavocat - rājan kathitaṃ mayā kālapuruṣa eṣa praviṣṭaḥ / na ca tvayā pramāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ vacanam / tasyaitat karmaphalamanubhava / tenātmānaṃ mahāpramāṇīkṛtam / tasya candrādityau skandhau vyavasthitau / gṛhītvāsau nigaḍacakradhanustomarabhiṇḍipālāsannahya (?) //

atha balirasurendro 'dhomukhaṃ prapatitaḥ smṛtibhraṣṭaḥ tharatharāyamānaḥ sthitaḥ / kiṃ kṛtya(?) svahastena mayā viṣaṃ bhakṣitam / dvipadāni paripūritāni / tṛtīyaṃ padaṃ na saṃvidyate / tadā sa kathayati - tṛtīyasya padaṃ na saṃvidyate / yanmama pratigrahaṃ yācitam, kīdṛśaṃ pāpaṃ karomyaham? atha nārāyaṇastametadavocat - yatrāhaṃ sthāpayāmi tatra tvayā sthātavyam / (
Vaidya 275

) atha sa balirasurendrastametadavocat - yādṛśaṃ tvayājñaptaṃ tādṛśaṃ karomyaham / satyaṃ kuruṣe? sa kathayati - satyaṃ satyaṃ karomyaham / tena satyapāśairbaddhaḥ / sā ca yajñabhūmirvināśitā / tāni ca bhāṇḍānyucchiṣṭīkṛtāni / tā api ca kumārikāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ kauravairvidhvaṃsitāḥ / tāni ca suvarṇamayāni siṃhāsanāni divyāni cchatrāṇyupānahāni ratnapariveṣṭitāni ca vastrābharaṇāni ca suvarṇaghaṇṭāni suvarṇakaṭakāni ratnakhacitāni kapilāni kauravapāṇḍavairvidhvaṃsitāni / sā ca yajñabhūmirvināśitā //

atha sa balirasurendro yajñabhūmerniṣkrāntaḥ śarīracintāmāpede - dātā balirudārayajñamupāsya / kāladānasya dattasya bandhanameva labdham / namo 'stu devāya / yathaiva kartā sartā sa nītvā pātālamupasthāpitaḥ sāntaḥpuraparivāraḥ / ākhyātaṃ hi mayā bhagavan - bhūtapūrvaṃ kurukṣetre mayā dānaṃ dattaṃ tasyaitatkarmaphalamanubhavāmi / tathā trātā bhavāhi me bhagavannātha, na bhūyo duḥkhamāpnuyām //

atha balistaṃ bhagavantamāryāvalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ stotraviśeṣaiḥ stotumārabdhaḥ - trāṇaṃ bhavāhi śubhapadmahasta / padmaśriyālaṃkṛtaśuddhakāya / amitābhamūrte śirasā namāmi / jaṭārdhamadhye cintāmaṇimukuṭadharāya / śubhapadmahastāya / padmaśriyā samalaṃkṛtāya / jaṭāmukuṭadharāya / sarvajñavaśīkṛtāya / bahusattvāśvāsanakarāya / hīnadīnānukampāya / dīvākaravararocanakarāya / pṛthivīvararocanakarāya / bhaiṣajyarājottamāya / suśuddhasattvāya / paramayogamanuprāptāya / mokṣapravarāya mokṣapriyāya / cintāmaṇivatsadṛśāya / dharmagañjaparipālanakarāya / ṣaṭpāramitānirdeśanakarāya / sucetanakarāya / idaṃ stotraṃ mayā kṛtamavalokiteśvarasya / sukhitāste sattvā ye tava nāmadheyamanusmaranti / mucyante te kārasūtrai rauravopapanneṣu avīcyupapanneṣu pretanagaropapanneṣu ye tava nāmadheyamanusmaranti / mucyante ta bahavaḥ pāpaduḥkhāt / sucetanāste sattvā ye tava nāmadheyamanusmaranti / gacchanti te sukhāvatīlokadhātum / amitābhasya tathāgatasya dharmamanusmaranti śṛṇvanti //

atha āryāvalokiteśvaro balerindrasya vyākaraṇamanuprayacchati sma - bhaviṣyasi tvamasurendra śrīrnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / sarve te 'surā vaineyā bhaviṣyanti / tatra tava buddhakṣetre na rāgaśabdo na dveṣaśabdo na mohaśabdo bhaviṣyati / ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā labdhalābhā bhaviṣyati / tena tasya dharmadakṣiṇā upanāmitā / śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāramupanāmitaṃ maulīkuṇḍalaṃ ca nānāratnasamuccitamupanāmitaṃ ca //

atha āryāvalokiteśvaro dharmadeśanāṃ kartumārabdhaḥ - śṛṇu mahārāja / nitye dhruve śāśvate mānuṣyake ye cintayanti satataparigrahaṃ mahābhogānyanuvicintayanti dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyān, yāni ca mahārhāṇi vastraśayyāsanāni, ye ca mahārhā nidhānadhanadhānadhanadhānyakoṣakoṣṭhāgārāḥ, ajñānāste sattvā ye putradāradārikāmanuvicintayanti bhāryāṃ mātāpitarau / (
Vaidya 276

) ebhirvastubhirye saktāste svapnopamā eva dṛśyante / maraṇakālasamaye na kaścitteṣāṃ trātā bhavati / yadā prāṇoddharaṇaṃ bhavati, tadā jambudvīpaṃ viparītaṃ paśyati / atha mahatīṃ vaitaraṇīṃ pūyaśoṇitaparipūrṇāṃ paśyanti / ye ca mahārhā vṛkṣāstān pradīptān saprajvalitānekajvālībhūtān paśyanti / dṛṣṭvā ca samāpadyante / tato yamapālapuruṣaiḥ kālapāśairbaddhvā nīyante / tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ kṣuradhāropacite mahāpathe pādā viśīryante / utkṣipte pāde ye 'nyāḥ pādāḥ prādurbhavanti, anekaiḥ kākagṛdhraśvānādibhirbhakṣyante / mahatīṃ nārakīyāṃ vedanāṃ pratyanubhavanti / tataḥ kṣuradhāropacitānmahāpathādavatīrya yatra ṣoḍaśāṅgulipramāṇāni kaṇṭakāni tatrānīyate, tata ekaikapāde pañca pañcaśatāni kaṇṭakāni praviśanti / sa cākrandanti - viṣayapāparatena sattvena karma kṛtam //

atha te yamapālapuruṣā evamāhuḥ - mārṣāḥ, na tvayā tathāgatasya piṇḍapātraṃ niryātitam / na ca tvayā dharmagaṇḍīmākoṭyamānā śrutā / na buddhanāma gṛhītam / na ca tvayā kvaciddānāni dīyamānāni dṛṣṭvānumoditāni / na ca tvayā kvacit pradeśe stūpabimbāni pradakṣiṇīkṛtāni / sa kathayati - aśrāddho 'bhūvaṃ pāparato buddhadharmasaṃghaparivarjitaḥ pāpamitraparigṛhītaḥ kalyāṇamitraparivarjitaśca / te kathayanti - tasyaitatkarmaphalamanubhavase / sa tairyamapālakairnīyate caitatkarmabhūmimupadarśayitum //
children.translated_text: Then those servants of <s>Yama</s> spoke thus: 'Sir, you did not offer alms-food to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Nor did you hear the <s>dharma</s>-bell being struck. You did not take the name of the <s>Buddha</s>. Nor did you, seeing gifts being given somewhere, rejoice in them. Nor did you circumambulate <s>stūpa</s> images at any place.' He said: 'I was without faith, devoted to evil, abandoned by the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>, seized by evil friends, and bereft of virtuous friends.' They said: 'You experience the fruit of that <s>karma</s>.' He was then led by those servants of <s>Yama</s> to be shown this realm of <s>karma</s>.

children.text: athe te yamapuruṣā nītvā kālasūtre mahānarake kṣipanti / śikṣā caikaikaśaktiśataṃ kāye vidhyanti tadapi jīvati, dvitīyaṃ śaktiśataṃ kāye vidhyanti tadapi jīvati, tṛtīyaṃ śaktiśataṃ kāye vidhyanti tadapi jīvati / yadā kalaṃ na kurvanti tadāgnikhadāmadhye kṣipanti / tadapi kālaṃ na kurvanti / tataste taptāyoguḍāmukhe viṣkambhante dahyante / teṣāmīṣṭamapi dantāni viśīryante, tālūni visphuṭante, kaṇṭhamapi tālumapi hṛdayamapi yantravatkalā nigaḍāyamānā sarvaṃ taṃ kāyaṃ dahyante / evameva hā rājan na kaścit trātā bhaviṣyati paraloke / tasmāttarhi taṃ mahārāja yatnena puṇyaṃ kartavyam / evaṃ sānulomikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtvā ca taṃ rājānaṃ balimasurendramevamāha - apramattena bhavitavyam, na punaḥ kadācitpramādacāriṇā bhavitavyam / evaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭo 'yaṃ gṛhāvāsaḥ paramadāruṇanarakabhūmiprapātanaḥ / tasmāttarhi mahārāja apramattena bhavitavyaṃ pāpabhīruṇā / paralokaṃ darśitam / api ca mahārāja / mamāntikāddharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇvato niravaśeṣāṇi pāpaskandhāni na ca supariśuddhāni / sarvaduḥkhataragāḍhabandhanaiḥ parimuktaḥ / sukhāvatīlokadhātugamanāya tava panthānaṃ pariśuddham / tatra ca tava saptaratnamayaṃ padmāsanaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati / yatra ratnapadme niṣadya tasya bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikāt imaṃ sarvaduḥkhapāpaskandhaṃ pāpaśamanaṃ sarvadurgatisādhanaṃ anantamaṇimahāpuṇyanirdeśaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānaṃ sūtraratnarājaṃ tvaṃ śroṣyasi, śrutvā ca tatraiva vyākaraṇamanuprāpsyase anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, tāvatsupariśuddhabodhicittālaṃkāraṃ nāma bodhisattvajanma pratilapsyase / yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho bhaviṣyasi //
children.translated_text: Then those servants of <s>Yama</s>, having led him, cast him into the great <s>Kālasūtra</s> (Black Thread) hell. They pierced his body with a hundred spears each, yet he still lived; they pierced his body with a second hundred spears, yet he still lived; they pierced his body with a third hundred spears, yet he still lived. When he did not die, they cast him into the midst of a fire-pit. Still he did not die. Then they forced molten iron balls into his mouth and burned him. His teeth crumbled, his palate split open, and his throat, palate, heart — all were crushed as if by a machine, and his entire body was burned. Thus, O King, there will be no protector in the next world. Therefore, O Great King, merit should be performed with effort. Having thus given a discourse on <s>Dharma</s> in due order, he spoke thus to King <s>Bali</s>, lord of <s>asuras</s>: 'One must be heedful, never again should one be given to heedlessness. This household life is so full of many faults, casting one down into the most terrible hells. Therefore, Great King, one must be heedful and fearful of sin. The next world has been shown to you. Moreover, Great King, by hearing the <s>Dharma</s> teaching from me, all your heaps of sin have been completely purified. You are freed from the bonds of all suffering and deep affliction. The path to the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Blissful) world-realm has been purified for you. There a lotus seat made of seven jewels will appear for you. Seated on that jewel-lotus, in the presence of the Blessed <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, you will hear this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha Mahāyāna Sūtratnarāja</s> (King of Jewel Sūtras), which extinguishes all sin, purifies all evil destinies, and expounds the infinite merit of the great jewel. Having heard it, you will there receive a prophecy of supreme perfect enlightenment, and you will attain the <s>bodhisattva</s> birth called <s>Supariśuddhabodhicittālaṃkāra</s> (Ornament of Completely Purified Mind of Awakening), until you become fully and perfectly enlightened in supreme <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 277

atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasya ca balerasurendrasya imaṃ sarvadurgatipariśodhanaṃ bodhisattvālaṃkārakāraṇḍavyūhaṃ nāma dharmālokaṃ deśayitvā taṃ rājānaṃ balimasurendraṃ samāśvāsya idamavocat - gamiṣyāmyaham / asmin jetavane mahāvihāre 'dya mahāsaṃnipāto bhavati //
children.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having taught to King <s>Bali</s>, lord of <s>asuras</s>, this <s>dharma</s>-light called <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-ornament that purifies all evil destinies, and having consoled that king, spoke thus: 'I shall depart. Today there is a great assembly at the <s>Jetavana</s> <s>mahāvihāra</s>.'

children.text: iti balisamāśvāsanaṃ nāmaikādaśaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter, called 'The Consolation of <s>Bali</s>.'

children.text: START Kvyu 1,12:
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s> 1.12]

children.text: yakṣādisamāśvāsanaṃ dvādaśaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The twelfth chapter, called 'The Consolation of <s>Yakṣas</s> and Others.'

children.text: tato 'valokiteśvareṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena raśmaya utsṛṣṭāḥ / anekāni nānāvarṇāni nīlapītalohitāvadātāni māñjiṣṭhasphaṭikarajatavarṇāni / gatvā ca viśvabhūvastathāgatasya purato vyavasthitāni / tadā te devā nāgā yakṣā rākṣasā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ / anekāni bodhisattvaśatāni saṃnipatitāni //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, emitted rays of light — of many and various colors: blue, yellow, red, white, madder, crystal, and silver. Having gone forth, they stood before <s>Viśvabhū</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then the <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and humans assembled. Hundreds of <s>bodhisattvas</s> assembled.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ bodhisattvenāṃ madhye gaganagañjo nāma bodhisattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - kuto bhagavan raśmaya āgacchanti? bhagavānāha - eṣa kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo balerasurendrasya bhavane viharati, tena tasmānniṣkrāmitvā amī raśmayaḥ pramuktāḥ / tato 'mī raśmaya āgacchanti, punastasyaiva sakāśaṃ gatāḥ //
children.translated_text: Then, from among those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Gaganagañja</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Whence, Blessed One, do these rays come?' The Blessed One said: 'This, O son of good family, is <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, who dwells in the palace of <s>Bali</s>, lord of <s>asuras</s>. Having departed from there, he released these rays. From there these rays come, and they have returned to his very presence.'

children.text: atha gaganagañjo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kenopāyena paśyeyamahamavalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam? bhagavānāha - eṣa kulaputra ihaivāgacchatyavalokiteśvaraḥ / yadā avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo balerasurendrasya bhavanānniṣkrāntaḥ, tadā jetavane mahāvihāre divyāni puṣpavarṣāṇi patanti, divyāni kalpavṛkṣaśatāni paramaśobhanīyāni, ratnālaṃkāraśatasahasrāṇi pralambitāni, muktāhāraśatasahasrāṇi pralambitāni, kāśikavastrasaccīvarāṇi pralambitāni, lohitadaṇḍāni suvarṇarūpyapatrāṇi anekāni puṣpavṛkṣaśatāni anekāni puṣkariṇīśatāni puṣpaparipūrṇāni paramaśobhanīyāni prādurbhūtāni //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Gaganagañja</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'By what means may I see <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'He, O son of good family, is coming here. When <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, has departed from the palace of <s>Bali</s>, lord of <s>asuras</s>, then in the <s>Jetavana</s> <s>mahāvihāra</s> divine showers of flowers will fall, hundreds of most beautiful divine <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees) will appear, hundreds of thousands of jewel ornaments will hang down, hundreds of thousands of pearl necklaces will hang down, fine <s>Kāśika</s> cloths and robes will hang down, red-stemmed trees with gold and silver leaves, hundreds of many flower trees, hundreds of many lotus ponds filled with flowers — all most beautiful — will appear.'

children.text: atha gaganagañjo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - nāgacchati bhagavannavalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ? bhagavānāha - eṣa kulaputra tato balerasurendrasya bhavanānniṣkamya paramabhīṣaṇīyaṃ tamondhakāraṃ nāma pṛthivīpradeśaṃ yakṣarākṣasānāṃ bhūmiṃ amanuṣyāvacaramapṛthivīpradeśaṃ tatra gacchati / yatra kulaputra candrādityau na jñāyete, tatra ca pṛthivīpradeśe varado nāma cintāmaṇiratnarājo 'sti / sa ca tatrāvabhāsaṃ kurute / anekāni yakṣarākṣasaśatasahasrāṇi tasmin dvīpe prativasanti / yadāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prativasati, tadā darśanamātrātsarvayakṣarākṣasāḥ paramahṛṣṭatuṣṭāḥ pramuditahṛdayā bhavanti / atha te 'valokiteśvarasya purastāddhāvanti, nirdhāvanti, dhāvitvā pādayoḥ praṇipatya saṃbhāṣayanti - mā tvaṃ bhagavan śrāntaklānto yastvaṃ cirakālena dṛṣṭaḥ, yastvamasyāṃ tamondhakārāyāṃ bhumau viharasi / (
Vaidya 278
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 278]

children.text: ) sa kathayati - anekāni kartavyāni me / na ca mayaikasattvasyārthe ātmabhāvaḥ pariniṣpāditaḥ / api tu sarvasattvānāmantike mayā mahākaruṇācittatotpādayitavyā //
children.translated_text: He said: 'I have many tasks to accomplish. Not for the sake of a single being alone have I brought this body to perfection. Rather, I must generate a mind of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇācitta</s>) toward all beings.'

Then <s>Gaganagañja</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Is <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, not coming, Blessed One?' The Blessed One said: 'He, O son of good family, having departed from the palace of <s>Bali</s>, lord of <s>asuras</s>, goes to a most terrifying region of earth called <s>Tamondhakāra</s> (Darkness), the land of <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, a non-human realm. Where, O son of good family, neither sun nor moon are known, in that region there is a wish-fulfilling jewel-king called <s>Varada</s> (Boon-giver). It illuminates that place. Hundreds of thousands of <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> dwell on that island. When <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, dwells there, then at the mere sight of him all the <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> become supremely joyful, delighted, with gladdened hearts. Then they run forth before <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, rush out, and having run, they prostrate at his feet and greet him: 'Do not be weary and tired, Blessed One, you whom we have seen after such a long time, you who dwell in this land of darkness.'

children.text: atha te sarve yakṣarākṣasā divyasuvarṇaratnamayaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ prasamayanti tasyāvalokiteśvarasyārthe vicitraiḥ puṣpamayaiḥ saṃchāditam, yatra ca bhagavānniṣadya dharmaṃ deśayati / sa tairyakṣarākṣasairnītvā tatra divyasuvarṇaratnamaye siṃhāsane viśrāmitaḥ / tataḥ avalokiteśvarasteṣāṃ yakṣarākṣasānāṃ dharma deśayati - śṛṇvattu bhavantaḥ / āryakāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya catuṣpādikāmapi gāthāṃ ye śroṣyanti, śrutvā ca dhārayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti pravartayiṣyanti, yoniśaṃ ca manasi kariṣyanti, teṣāmidaṃ puṇyaskandhasaṃcodano bhaviṣyati / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāḥ śakyaṃ mayā paramāṇurajasāṃ pramāṇamudgrahītum, na tu kulaputrāḥ śakyaṃ mayā kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāḥ śakyaṃ mayā mahāsamudrasyaikamudakabinduṃ gaṇayitum, na tu kulaputrāḥ śakyaṃ mayā kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya catuṣpādikāyā api gāthāyāḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāḥ dvādaśagaṅgānadīvālukopamāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhādvādaśakalpānekasthāne dhārayeyuḥ, cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajaghaṇṭāpatākābhiḥ, te 'pi tathāgatāḥ sarve sahitā bhūtvā kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya catuṣpādikāyā api gāthāyāḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayituṃ na śaknuvanti sma, prāgevāhamekākī tamondhakārabhūmau viharāmi //
children.translated_text: Then all those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> prepared a divine golden jeweled lion-throne for <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, covered with various flowers, where the Blessed One sat and taught the <s>Dharma</s>. He was led by those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> and made to rest upon that divine golden jeweled lion-throne. Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> to those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>: 'Listen, noble ones! Those who will hear even a single four-lined verse of the <s>Āryakāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, and having heard it, will retain it, master it, propagate it, and wisely reflect upon it in their minds — for them this mass of merit shall be set in motion. Just as, O sons of good family, it is possible for me to count the measure of atoms of dust, but it is not possible for me, O sons of good family, to calculate the mass of merit of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>. Just as, O sons of good family, it is possible for me to count a single drop of water in the great ocean, but it is not possible for me, O sons of good family, to calculate the mass of merit of even a four-lined verse of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>. Just as, O sons of good family, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, equal in number to the sands of twelve <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, were to be sustained in one place for twelve <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, medicines for the sick, flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags — even all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> together would not be able to calculate the mass of merit of even a four-lined verse of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, how much less could I alone, dwelling in this realm of utter darkness!'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāścaturmahādvīpeṣvekaikadvīpapramāṇaṃ gṛhaṃ vihāraṃ vā kārayeddivyasuvarṇaratnamayam, tatra gṛhe vihāre vā stūpasahasraṃ kuryāt, teṣāṃ caikadine dhātvāvaropaṇaṃ kuryāt, yacca teṣāṃ dhātvāvaropaṇeṣu pūjāyāṃ puṇyaskandham, tato bahutaraṃ kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya catuṣpādikāyā api gāthāyāḥ puṇyaskandham / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāḥ pañca mahānadyo sahasranadīparivārā mahāsamudramupasaṃkrāmanti, evameva kulaputrā asya kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānasūtraratnarājasya catuṣpādikāmapi gāthāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ puṇyaughapravāhamupapravahati //
children.translated_text: Just as, O sons of good family, if one were to build in each of the four great continents a house or a monastery the size of the continent, made of divine gold and jewels, and in that house or monastery were to erect a thousand <s>stūpas</s>, and in a single day were to install relics in each of them — whatever mass of merit there would be from the worship of those relic installations, far greater than that is the mass of merit of even a four-lined verse of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>. Just as, O sons of good family, the five great rivers with their retinue of a thousand rivers flow into the great ocean, even so, O sons of good family, a flood of merit flows forth for those who hear even a four-lined verse of this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>.

children.text: atha te yakṣarākṣasā avalokiteśvarametadavocan - ye sattvāḥ kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ likhāpayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ kidṛśaṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ bhavati? sa āha - aprameyaṃ teṣāṃ kulaputrāḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ prabhavati / ye kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ likhāpayanti, taiścaturaśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇi likhāpiutāni bhavanti / te rājāno bhavanti, cakravartinaścaturdvīpeśvarā bhavanti / te sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānāṃ janayanti / ye satataparigrahaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya nāmamanusmaranti, mucyante te īdṛśātsaṃsārikādduḥkhāt / jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevanāduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaparimukta bhavanti / yatra yatropapadyante, tatra tatra jātau jātau jātismarā bhavanti / (
Vaidya 279
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 279]

children.text: ) teṣāṃ ca kāyāt gośīrṣacandanagandho vāsyati / nīlotpalagandhino mukhā bhavanti / paripūrṇagātrāśca bhavanti / mahānagnā aparimāṇapuṇyabalasamanvāgatāśca te satpurūṣā bhaviṣyanti / na kadācit yakṣatvaṃ na rākṣasatvaṃ na pretatvaṃ na piśācatvaṃ na pūtanātvaṃ na kaṭapūtanātvaṃ na manuṣyadāridryaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyanti / gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sevāpuṇyaskandhena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti / ye 'pi kecit kulaputrāḥ sattvā asmāt kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānasūtraratnarājādekākṣaramapi nāmadheyamapi catuṣpādikāmapi gāthāṃ likhāpayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ gamiṣyanti / te cābhirūpā bhaviṣyanti / prāsādikā bhaviṣyanti / darśanīyāśca bhaviṣyanti / bahujanapriyamanāpadarśanena ca bhaviṣyanti / teṣāṃ na kaścit kāye vyādhiḥ prabhaviṣyati / na cakṣurogaṃ na śrotrarogaṃ na ghrāṇarogaṃ na jihvārogaṃ na kāyarogam / na hīnāṅgāni bhaviṣyanti / na pratyantikeṣu janapadeṣu pratyājāyante / na mleccheṣu na pāpakuleṣu norabhrikeṣu na kaukkuṭikeṣu na jatyeṣu(?) pratyājāyante / supariśuddhakāyāśca te satpuruṣā bhaviṣyanti //
children.translated_text: From their bodies emanates the fragrance of <s>gośīrṣa</s> (ox-head) sandalwood. Their mouths become fragrant like blue lotuses. They become complete in all limbs, greatly powerful, and endowed with immeasurable merit and strength — such noble beings they shall become. Never will they experience the state of a <s>yakṣa</s>, nor that of a <s>rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), nor a <s>piśāca</s> (demon), nor a <s>pūtanā</s> (corpse-demon), nor a <s>kaṭapūtanā</s> (flesh-eating demon), nor the poverty of a human. They shall be endowed with a mass of merit equal to the service of <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones numbering as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. And whoever, O sons of good family, among beings shall cause even a single syllable, even the name, even a four-lined verse to be written from this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s> — for them the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) karmas shall be completely exhausted. They shall be handsome. They shall be graceful. They shall be beautiful to behold. They shall be beloved and pleasing in appearance to many people. No disease whatsoever shall afflict their bodies — no eye disease, no ear disease, no nose disease, no tongue disease, no bodily disease. They shall not have deficient limbs. They shall not be reborn in border regions, nor among barbarians, nor in sinful families, nor among butchers, nor among poultry-keepers, nor among outcastes. Such noble beings shall have perfectly purified bodies.

Then those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> said this to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: 'What kind of mass of merit will accrue to those beings who cause the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, to be written down?' He replied: 'Immeasurable, O sons of good family, is the mass of merit that arises for them. Those who cause the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, to be written, by them the eighty-four thousand collections of <s>Dharma</s> (dharma-skandhas) have been caused to be written. They become kings, universal monarchs (<s>cakravartins</s>) ruling over the four continents. They beget a thousand sons — heroes, mighty warriors, of splendid form, crushers of enemy armies. Those who constantly remember and cherish the name of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, are liberated from such <s>saṃsāric</s> (worldly) suffering. They become freed from birth, old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, pain, mental anguish, and despair. Wherever they are reborn, in each and every birth they possess the memory of past lives.

children.text: atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ teṣāṃ yakṣarākṣasānāṃ tamondhakāravāsināṃ sarveṣāṃ cānulomikāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān / te yakṣarākṣasāstāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śubhāṃ śrutvā kecit srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhitāḥ / kecit sakṛdāgāmiphale, kecidanāgamiphale, kecidarhattve, kecit prabhutvabodhau pratiṣṭhitāḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having thus delivered a <s>Dharma</s> teaching suited to each of those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> dwelling in utter darkness — upon hearing that excellent <s>Dharma</s> teaching, some of those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> became established in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>), some in the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), some in the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>), some in <s>arhatship</s> (liberation), and some became established in the awakening of sovereignty.

children.text: ato yenāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tenopasaṃkramya pādayoḥ praṇipatya evaṃ kathayanti - ihaiva bhagavan viharasva, mānyatra sthāne kvacidgaccha, vayaṃ te upasthānaparicaryāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, vayaṃ ca tavāntike asminneva tamondhakārabhūmau tavārthāya divyāni sauvarṇamayāni caṃkramaṇāni kariṣyāmaḥ / mā bhagavannanyatra pradeśaṃ gacchasva, vayaṃ tavādarśanāt kathaṃ tiṣṭhāmaḥ? atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāṃśca yakṣarākṣasānetadavocat - anekāni ca mayā kulaputrāḥ sattvāni bodhimārge niyojayitavyāni / atha te sarve yakṣarākṣasāḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparā vyavasthitāḥ / te parasparamevamāhuḥ - gamiṣyati ayamasmākamavalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nyataraṃ pṛthivīpradeśam, tadvayaṃ dharmasāṃkathyaviprahīṇā bhaviṣyāmaḥ / kimasmābhiḥ kartavyam? atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāstamondhakārāyā bhūmyāḥ saṃprasthitaḥ / atha te tamondhakāraprativāsino yakṣarākṣasāstasya bhagavato 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchanti sma / atha avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastānetadavocat - pratinivartayadhvam / dūratamevamāha(?) //
children.translated_text: Then they approached the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, prostrated at his feet, and spoke thus: 'Remain here, O Blessed One! Do not go to any other place. We shall perform attendance and service for you. We shall build for you, in your honor, divine golden promenades here in this very realm of utter darkness. Do not go to another place, O Blessed One! How shall we endure without seeing you?' Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, said this to those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>: 'Many beings, O sons of good family, must be set upon the path of awakening by me.' Then all those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, resting their cheeks upon their hands, stood absorbed in grief. They said to one another: 'This <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, will depart to another region of the earth, and we shall be bereft of <s>Dharma</s> conversation. What shall we do?' Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, set forth from that realm of utter darkness. Then those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> dwelling in utter darkness followed close behind the Blessed <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, going after him step by step. Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, said to them: 'Turn back! You have come far enough.'

children.text: te yakṣarākṣasāḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya tatraiva ca prakrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: Those <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, having bowed their heads at his feet and circumambulated him three times, departed to that very place.

children.text: iti yakṣādisamāśvāsanaṃ nāma dvādaśaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter, called 'The Consolation of the <s>Yakṣas</s> and Others.'

children.text: Vaidya 280
devabhavanabhramaṇaṃ trayodaśaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The thirteenth chapter: 'The Wandering through the Celestial Abodes.'

children.text: athāryāvalokiteśvaro jvaladivāgnipiṇḍamākāśe 'ntarhitaḥ / tato devabhavanaṃ gatvā śuddhāvāsakāyikadevaputrāṇāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya brāhmaṇarūpamātmānamabhinirmāyāgamat / tatra devanikāyeṣu sukuṇḍalo nāma devaputro daridro duścittaśceti / atha āryāvalokiteśvaraḥ sa tena brāhmaṇarūpeṇa tasya devaputrasya sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ dāridryaduḥkhavyupaśamāya taṃ devaputrametadavocat - bubhukṣito 'haṃ tṛṣitaśceti / atha sa devaputro rudaṃstaṃ brāhmaṇametadavocat - na ca me brāhmaṇa kiṃcitsaṃvidyate / brāhmaṇo 'vocat - avaśyaṃ tvayā mama kiṃciddātavyam / atha sa devaputro vimānaṃ praviśya sarvabhāṇḍaṃ nirabhyavekṣitumārabdhaḥ / sa ca paripatitaṃ niveśanaṃ divyairmahārhai ratnabhāṇḍaiḥ paripūrṇaṃ dakṣiṇapārśvam, anyāni ca bhāṇḍāni divyarasarasāgropetairāhāraiḥ paripūrṇāni vāmapārśve vimānasya vastrābharaṇaiḥ sarvapuṣpagandhādibhiḥ paripūrṇāni //
children.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, blazing like a mass of fire, disappeared into the sky. From there he went to the celestial realm and approached the <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) of the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) heaven. Having approached, he manifested himself in the form of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and went there. Among those divine hosts, there was a <s>devaputra</s> named <s>Sukuṇḍala</s>, who was poor and dejected. Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, in that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> form, approached that <s>devaputra</s>. Having approached, in order to alleviate the suffering of poverty of all the <s>devas</s>, he spoke thus to that <s>devaputra</s>: 'I am hungry and thirsty.' Then that <s>devaputra</s>, weeping, said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: 'I have nothing at all, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'You must give me something.' Then that <s>devaputra</s> entered his celestial palace and began to search through all his possessions. He found that his dilapidated dwelling was now filled with divine, most precious jewel-vessels on the right side, and other vessels filled with food of supreme divine flavors on the left side of the palace, along with garments, ornaments, and all manner of flowers and fragrances.

children.text: atha sa devaputra etad dṛṣṭaivaṃ cintāmāpede - avaśyamayaṃ sa satpātro dvāre sthito yasya darśanamātreṇāpidṛśī lakṣmīrmamānuprāptā / atha sa devaputrastaṃ brāhmaṇamāhūyaivamāha - ehi brāhmaṇa, idaṃ vimānaṃ praviśa / sa ca brāhmaṇastena devaputreṇa vimāne praviśya tairdivyaratnaiḥ pratipāditaḥ, divyai rasarasāgropetairāhārairbhojitaḥ, divyairvastraiḥ pravāritaḥ / sa bhuktvā ca svastikāramanukurute / atha sa devaputrastaṃ brāhmaṇametadavocat - bho brāhmaṇa, katamāyā bhūmyāstvamāgataḥ? brāhmaṇa āha - jetavananāmamahāvihārādahamāgataḥ / atha sa devaputrastametadavocat - kīdṛśī sā bhūmiḥ? atha sa brāhmaṇo devaputrametadavocat - tathāgatādhyuṣitā sā bhūmī ramaṇīyā divyamaṇiratnaparikhacitā pariśobhitā / paribhogāya ca tadbhūmau divyakalpavṛkṣāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ, manoramāṇi puṣpāṇi prādubharvanti, vividhāḥ puṣkariṇyo dṛśyante, vividhāśca śīlavanto guṇavanto dakṣiṇīyā dṛśyante viśvabhuvaḥ / tathāgatasyānekāni prātihāryāṇi dṛśyante / evaṃ sā paramaramaṇīyā devaputra bhūmiḥ / atha sa devaputrastaṃ brāhmaṇametadavocat - avaśyaṃ tvayā brāhmaṇa satyaṃ pratyāhāraḥ kartavyaḥ / athavā tvaṃ devo 'si, manuṣyo 'si vā? na ca manuṣyasyedṛśaṃ nimittaṃ bhavati yādṛśaṃ tava nimittaṃ bhavati / atha sa brāhmaṇastametadavocat - na devaḥ, api tu mānuṣo 'haṃ bodhisattvabhūtaḥ / evaṃ hīnadīnānukampako bodhimārgamupadarśakaḥ / atha sa devaputrastasmai maulikuṇḍalamupanāmayati, upanāmayitvā ca sa devaputra imāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣita(vān) -
children.translated_text: Then that <s>devaputra</s>, having seen this, thought thus: 'Surely this worthy one standing at the door is a vessel of merit, by the mere sight of whom such fortune has come to me.' Then that <s>devaputra</s> invited the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and said: 'Come, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, enter this palace.' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> entered the palace with that <s>devaputra</s> and was presented with those divine jewels, fed with food of supreme divine flavors, and clothed with divine garments. Having eaten, he made the gesture of blessing. Then that <s>devaputra</s> said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: 'O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, from which land have you come?' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'I have come from the great monastery called <s>Jetavana</s>.' Then the <s>devaputra</s> said: 'What is that land like?' Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said to the <s>devaputra</s>: 'That land is inhabited by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it is delightful, adorned and embellished with divine jewels. For enjoyment, divine <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees) have appeared on that land, beautiful flowers bloom, various lotus ponds are seen, and various persons of good conduct, virtue, and worthy of offerings are seen — of <s>Viśvabhū</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, many miracles are seen. Thus, O <s>devaputra</s>, that land is supremely delightful.' Then the <s>devaputra</s> said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: 'You must truthfully confess, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Are you a <s>deva</s> or a human? For a human does not have such signs as you possess.' Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'I am not a <s>deva</s>, but I am a human who has become a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Thus I show compassion to the lowly and wretched, and I reveal the path to enlightenment.' Then the <s>devaputra</s> offered his crest-jewel earring to him, and having offered it, the <s>devaputra</s> spoke this verse:

children.text: aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, what a field of merit, free from all faults!

children.text: adyaiva vāpitaṃ bījaṃ adyaiva phalasaṃpadam //
children.translated_text: The seed sown today yields its fruit this very day.'

children.text: atha sa devaputra imāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣitvā tatraiva prakrāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>devaputra</s>, having spoken this verse, departed from that very place.

children.text: iti devabhavanabhramaṇaṃ nāma trayodaśaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, called 'The Wandering through the Celestial Abodes.'

children.text: START Kvyu 1,14:
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s> 1.14]

children.text: Vaidya 281
siṃhalabhramaṇaṃ caturdaśaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The fourteenth chapter: 'The Wandering through <s>Siṃhala</s> (Lanka).'

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇaḥ tasmāddevanikāyādavatīrya siṃhaladvīpaṃ pratyudgataḥ / gatvā ca rākṣasīnāṃ purato vyavasthitaḥ kāmarūpamātmānamabhinirmāya prāsādikam / atha tā rākṣasyo 'nyonyamevamāhuḥ - ayamīdṛśaṃ paramakāmarūpī puruṣo dṛśyate / atha taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca tadā tāsāṃ rākṣasīnāṃ kāmacittamutpannam / tadā tasya sakāśamupasaṃkramyaitadavocan - bhavāṃstvaṃ bhajasva asmākaṃ kumārīyauvanam, na cāsmākaṃ svāmī saṃvidyate / tvaṃ ca bho puruṣa, asvāmikānāṃ svāmī bhava / agatikānāṃ gatirbhava / aparāyaṇānāṃ parayāṇo bhava / atrāṇānāṃ trāṇaṃ bhava / advīpānāṃ dvīpo bhava / andhānāmāloko bhava / imāni te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi vividhāni vicitrāṇi śayanāni udyānaramaṇīyāni puṣkiriṇīramayāṇi //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having descended from that celestial host, proceeded to <s>Siṃhala</s> island. Having gone there, he stood before the <s>rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses), manifesting himself in the most attractive and pleasing form. Then those <s>rākṣasīs</s> said to one another: 'Such a man of supremely attractive form is seen.' Having seen him, desire arose in those <s>rākṣasīs</s>. Then, approaching him, they said: 'Please enjoy the youth of our maidens, for we have no husband. O man, be the husband of us who are without husbands. Be the refuge of us who are without refuge. Be the shelter of us who are without shelter. Be the protector of us who are without protection. Be the island of us who are without an island. Be the light of us who are blind. Here are our food-houses, drink-houses, garment-houses, various and wonderful couches, delightful gardens, and lovely lotus ponds.'

children.text: sa kathayati - madīyamājñaptaṃ yadi kurute, tatsarvaṃ yuṣmākaṃ yathābhiprāyaṃ kariṣyāmi / tāśca tamāhuḥ - kathaṃ vayaṃ tavājñāṃ na kariṣyāmaḥ? tena tāsāmāryāṣṭāṅgikamārgamupadarśitam / daśa kuśalāni karmapathānyupadarśitāni / āgamacatuṣṭayaṃ cādhītam / atha tā rākṣasyastasyapuruṣasyāntikādāryāṣṭāṅgikamārgaṃ gṛhītvā daśa kuśalāni ca saṃsmarya, satyacatuṣṭayaṃ prāptvā, āgamasatyacatuṣṭayādhītāḥ, kāścitsrotāpattiphalamanuprāptāḥ, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ cānuprāptāḥ, anāgāmiphalaṃ cānuprāptāḥ, yāvatkāścidarhattvaṃ kāścitpratyekabodhimanuprāptāḥ, tadā tāsāṃ rākṣasīnāṃ rāgaduḥkhaṃ na bādhate / dveṣaduḥkhaṃ na bādhate / mohaduḥkhaṃ na bādhate / āghātacittaṃ na bhavati / na ca kasyacijjīvitāntarāyaṃ kurvanti / abhiratā dharmeṣu vyavasthitāḥ, śikṣāsaṃvaramupagṛhītāḥ / evaṃ cāhuḥ - punarapi na prāṇātipātaṃ kurvāmaḥ / yādṛśena jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā jīvanti annena pānena, tādṛśajīvikayā vayaṃ jīvāmaḥ / punarapi rākṣasīvṛttiṃ na kurvāmaḥ / upāsakasaṃvaraṃ dhārayiṣyāma iti / tādṛśaṃ śikṣāsaṃvaramupagṛhītvā tasyaiva puruṣasya purato 'nimiṣairnayanaiḥ prekṣamāṇāḥ prasthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: He said: 'If you follow my instructions, then I shall do everything according to your wishes.' They said: 'How could we not follow your instructions?' Then he taught them the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>). He showed them the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśa kuśalāni karmapathāni</s>). The four <s>āgamas</s> (collections of teachings) were studied. Then those <s>rākṣasīs</s>, having received the Noble Eightfold Path from that man and having remembered the ten wholesome deeds, having attained the four truths, and having studied the four truths of the <s>āgamas</s> — some attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>), some attained the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), some attained the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), and some even attained <s>arhatship</s>, and some attained <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary enlightenment). Then those <s>rākṣasīs</s> were no longer afflicted by the suffering of desire, no longer afflicted by the suffering of hatred, no longer afflicted by the suffering of delusion. No thoughts of malice arose. They did not endanger anyone's life. Delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>, they were established in it and took up the training and discipline. They declared: 'Never again shall we take life. We shall live by the same kind of food and drink by which the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> live. Never again shall we follow the ways of <s>rākṣasīs</s>. We shall uphold the lay-disciple's vows (<s>upāsakasaṃvara</s>).' Having taken up such training and discipline, they departed, gazing without blinking at that very man.

children.text: iti siṃhalabhramaṇaṃ nāma caturdaśaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, called 'The Wandering through <s>Siṃhala</s>.'

children.text: START Kvyu 1,15:
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s> 1.15]

children.text: vārāṇasībhramaṇaṃ pañcadaśaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The fifteenth chapter: 'The Wandering through <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.'

children.text: atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasmātsiṃhaladvīpādavatīrya vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryāmuccāraprasrāvasthāne gato yatrānekānyanekāni kṛmikulaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti / tato 'valokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva upasaṃkramya tatrāsa tāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi dṛṣṭvā ātmānaṃ bhramararūpamabhinirmāya ghuṇaghuṇāyamāṇam / tadeṣāṃ śabdaṃ niścārayati - namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namaḥ saṃghāya iti / tacchrutvā te ca sarve prāṇakāḥ namo buddhāya namo dharmāya namaḥ saṃghāyeti nāmamanusmārayanti / te ca sarve buddhanāmasmaraṇamātreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā sarve te sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapannāḥ sugandhamukhā nāma bodhisattvā babhūvuḥ / sarve te bhagavato 'mitābhasya tathāgatasyāntikādidaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ nāma mahāyānaṃ śrutvā anumodya ca nānādigbhyo vyākaraṇāni pratilabdhāni //
children.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having descended from that <s>Siṃhala</s> island, went to a place of excrement and urine in the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, where many hundreds of thousands of worm-families dwelled. Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having approached and seeing those hundreds of thousands of creatures, manifested himself in the form of a bee, buzzing. He produced this sound: '<s>Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namaḥ Saṃghāya</s>' (Homage to the Buddha, Homage to the Dharma, Homage to the Saṅgha). Hearing this, all those creatures called to mind: '<s>Namo Buddhāya, Namo Dharmāya, Namaḥ Saṃghāya</s>.' By the mere recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>'s name, all of them, having split with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable body that rises with twenty peaks, were reborn in the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-realm and became <s>bodhisattvas</s> named <s>Sugandhamukha</s> (Fragrant-faced). All of them, having heard this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha Mahāyāna</s> in the presence of the Blessed <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> and having rejoiced, received prophecies from various directions.

children.text: Vaidya 282
atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo sattvaparipākaṃ kṛtvā tasyā vārāṇasyā mahānagaryāḥ prakrāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having ripened those beings, departed from that great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: iti vārāṇasībhramaṇaṃ nāma pañcadaśaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, called 'The Wandering through <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.'

children.text: START Kvyu 1,16:
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s> 1.16]

children.text: magadhabhramaṇaṃ ṣoḍaśaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The sixteenth chapter: 'The Wandering through <s>Magadha</s>.'

children.text: tadā sa magadhābhimukhaṃ pratyudgacchati / sa magadhaviṣayamanuprāptaḥ / yāvat sattvān paśyanti sma parasparaṃ māṃsabhakṣaṇaṃ kurvāṇān / atha āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastānevamāha - kasmādbhoḥ, yūyaṃ anyonyaṃ māsaṃ bhakṣayatha? te cāhuḥ - nādyaiva māsaṃbhakṣaṇam, viṃśativarṣāṇi paripūrṇāni kāntārasya ca pratipannasya ca / nātra kiṃcidannapānaṃ saṃvidyate / tasmādvayaṃ anyonyaṃ virodhaṃ kurvāṇā jīvitāḥ / evaṃ kṛtvā māṃsabhakṣaṇaṃ kurvāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then he proceeded toward <s>Magadha</s>. He arrived in the <s>Magadha</s> region. There he saw beings devouring each other's flesh. Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, spoke to them thus: 'Why, sirs, do you eat one another's flesh?' They said: 'This flesh-eating is not just of today — twenty full years have passed since we entered this wilderness and set forth on this path. There is no food or drink to be found here. Therefore, fighting one another, we have survived. Thus we eat flesh.'

children.text: atha avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvaścintāmāpede - kenopāyenāhaṃ sattvān sarvān sukhopadhānaistasmātkāntārānmahādārūṇādakālamaraṇātparimocayeyaṃ saṃtarpayeyam? athāvalokiteśvaro vividhāni varṣāṇi pravarṣitumārabdhaḥ / prathamamudakavarṣam / yadā udakena saṃtarpitāḥ prīṇitagātrāśca bhavanti, tadā paścāddivyāni piṣṭakāni rasarasāgropetāni tenāhāreṇa paripūrṇāni / yadāhāreṇa saṃtarpitā bhavanti tadā dhānyavarṣāṇi patanti, anyāni ca tilataṇḍulakolamudgamāṣakalāvamasūrayavagodhūmaśālidhānyakulatthādīni patanti sma / vividhāni ca vastrābharaṇāni ca pravarṣanti sma / yadā yadā teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ ke 'pyabhiprāyā bhavanti, tadā tadā teṣāṃ sattvānāmabhiprāyā anusidhyante / atha te māgadhakāḥ sattvāstadidaṃ vicitraṃ svātmasukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhaṃ ca vyupaśāntam, tadā paramavismayamāpannāḥ / te ca sarve ekasthāne viśrāntāḥ, viśramitvā parasparamevamāhuḥ - kasya devasyāyaṃ prabhāvaḥ? tatasteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ madhye jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ kubjo gopāṇasīvakro 'dhibhagno dāṇḍaparāyaṇaḥ anekavarṣaśatasahasrāyuṣikaḥ / sa teṣāṃ madhye sthitvā kathayati - na yuṣmākamanyadevasya kasyacidīdṛśaṃ prabhāvo bhavati virahitādavalokiteśvarasya / tatastā parṣadaḥ pṛcchanti - kīdṛśaṃ tasya nimittamavalokiteśvarasya? atha sa puruṣa āryāvalokiteśvarasya guṇodbhāvanāṃ bhāṣitumārabdhaḥ -
children.translated_text: Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, thought to himself: 'By what means shall I liberate and nourish all beings from that terrible wilderness of untimely death, with provisions of happiness?' Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> caused various rains to fall,

children.text: śṛṇuta kulaputrāḥ / avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'ndhabhūtānāṃ dīpabhūtaḥ, sūryatāpadagdhānāṃ chatrībhūtaḥ, tṛṣopadrutānāṃ nadībhūtaḥ, bhayabhītānāmabhayaṃdadaḥ, vyādhiparipīḍitānāṃ vaidyabhūtaḥ, duḥkhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ mātāpitṛbhūtaḥ, avīcyupapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ nirvāṇapradarśakaḥ / īdṛśāni bhavantastasya guṇaviśeṣāṇi / sukhitāste sattvā loke ye tasya nāmamanusmaranti / te āpaścimaṃ sāṃsārikaṃ duḥkhaṃ parivarjayanti / sacetanāste puruṣapuṃgavā ye avalokiteśvarasya satataparigrahaṃ puṣpadhūpaṃ niryātayanti / ye 'valokiteśvarasya purataścaturasraṃ maṇḍalakaṃ kurvanti, te rājāno bhavanti cakravartinaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgatāḥ / tadyathā - cakraratnam, aśvaratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnam / evaṃ sapta ratnāni, ebhiḥ saptaratnaiḥ samanvāgatā bhavanti / ye cāvalokiteśvarasyaikamapi puṣpaṃ niryātayanti, te (
Vaidya 283
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 283]

children.text: ) sugandhikāyā bhavanti / yatra yatropapadyante tatra tatra parīpūrṇakāyāśca bhavanti / evaṃ sa puruṣo guṇaviśeṣaṃ kṛtavāna / tāśca parṣadaḥ svakasvakeṣu bhavaneṣu pratyudgatāḥ, anantavimalā nāma kāyapariśuddhiḥ [tāṃ] pratilabhante sma / atha sa jīrṇapurūṣaḥ ānulomikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtvā svakaṃ gṛhaṃ niveśanaṃ pratyudgataḥ / athāvalokiteśvarastatraivākāśe 'ntarhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: They become fragrant. Wherever they are reborn, there they become complete in body. Thus did that man accomplish special virtues. And those assemblies returned to their respective abodes, [their bodies being called] <s>Anantavimalā</s> (Infinite Purity).

Listen, O sons of good family! <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, is a lamp for the blind, an umbrella for those scorched by the heat of the sun, a river for those afflicted by thirst, a bestower of fearlessness to the frightened, and a physician for those tormented by disease.

children.text: atha sa ākāśe cintāmāpede - viśvabhūstathāgato me cirakālaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ, so 'nupūrveṇa jetavanaṃ vihāramanupraviṣṭaḥ / yāvatpaśyati anekāni devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi / anekāni ca bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni //
children.translated_text: Then he thought while in the sky: 'Long ago I saw the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Viśvabhū</s>, and he has gradually entered the <s>Jetavana</s> <s>vihāra</s> (monastery).' Then he saw many hundreds of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans.

children.text: atha gaganagañjo bodhisattvo bhagavantametadavocat - katamo 'yaṃ bhagavan bodhisattva āgacchati? bhagavānāha - eṣa kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva āgacchati / atha gaganagañjo bodhisattvaḥ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ / athāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvastaṃ bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vāmapārśve viśrāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganagañja</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Who is this <s>bodhisattva</s> who comes, O Blessed One?' The Blessed One replied: 'This, O son of good family, is <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, who comes.' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganagañja</s>,

children.text: atha sa punaḥ śrāntaṃ viditvā bhagavān pṛcchati - śrāntastvaṃ kulaputra / kīdṛśī karmabhūmistvayā niṣpāditāḥ? tana tasya bhūtapūrvaṃ varṇitam - sadā preteṣvavīcyupapanneṣu kālasūtrarauravopapanneṣu hāhe tapane mahānarake, sitodake mahānarake, asicchede mahānarake, saṃvare mahānarake / eṣu mahānarakeṣu ye sattvā upapannāsteṣāṃ ca karmabhūmiḥ sattvānāmaparipākakṛtā kartavyā, kṛtvā cānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāḥ / īdṛśo mayā sattvaparipākaḥ kṛtaḥ / atha gaganagañjo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ paramavismayamāpannaḥ - na ca me bodhisattvabhūtasya īdṛśaṃ viṣayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śruta vā, tathāgatānāmīdṛśaṃ viṣayaṃ na saṃvidyate //
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing him to be weary, again asked: 'Are you weary, O son of good family? What kind of field of action have you accomplished?' Then his former deeds were described: 'Always among the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), among those reborn in <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell), among those born in <s>Kālasūtra</s> (the Black Thread hell) and <s>Raurava</s> (the Screaming hell) — alas!'

children.text: athe gaganagañjo bodhisattvo 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya purataḥ sthitvā avalokiteśvaramevamāha - mā tvaṃ śrāntaḥ / kliṣṭastvam / sa āha - na cāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ madhye śrānto na kliṣṭaḥ / tau parasparaṃ sāṃkathyaṃ kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitau //
children.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gaganagañja</s>, standing before the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, said to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: 'Are you not weary? Are you not afflicted?' He replied: 'I am neither weary nor afflicted among you all.'

children.text: atha bhagavān ṣaṭpāramitānirdeśaṃ dharmaṃ deśayitumārabdhaḥ - śṛṇvantu kulaputrāḥ / prathamaṃ bodhisattvabhūtena dānapāramitā paripūrayitavyā / evaṃ śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā dhai(vī)ryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā paripūrayitavyā / imāṃ cānulomikāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ / atha tāḥ parṣadaḥ svakasvakasthāneṣu prakrāntāḥ, te ca bodhisattvāḥ svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu prakrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One began to teach the <s>Dharma</s> exposition of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections): 'Listen, O sons of good family! First, one who is a <s>bodhisattva</s> must perfect <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (the perfection of giving). Likewise <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (the perfection of moral conduct), <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (the perfection of patience), <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> (the perfection of vigor), <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (the perfection of meditation),

children.text: ayaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānasūtraratnarājasya prathamo nirvyūhaḥ sarvakarmaviśodhano 'nuttarabodhimārgapratiṣṭhāpakaḥ samāptaḥ // 1 //

children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Tell us, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, of the <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions) formerly attained by <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, by which <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> was absorbed." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "<s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is endowed with immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>samādhis</s>, the limit of which cannot be fathomed even by all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>." Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> said: "Describe those <s>samādhis</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, out of compassion for all beings." children.text: Vaidya 285

bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra ahaṃ siṃhalarājo nāma bodhisattvabhūto 'bhūvam / tato 'haṃ siṃhaladvīpayātrāṃ saṃprasthitaḥ / pañcabhirvaṇikputraśataiḥ sārdhaṃ śakaṭairbhārairmūṭaiḥ piṭharairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhādibhiḥ prabhūtaṃ paṇyamāropya siṃhaladvīpaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ / tato 'nupūrveṇa grāmanagaranigamaparṇapattaneṣu caṃcūryamāṇaḥ siṃhaladvīpamanuprāptaḥ, yena nipuṇaṃ tadyānapātraṃ pratipāditam / tadā me karṇadhārā āhuḥ - kathaya kathaya yuṣmākaṃ katamadvīpeṣu gamanāyedṛśā vāyavo vānti? athavā ratnadvīpeṣu vāyavo vānti, athavā rākṣasadvīpeṣu vāyavo vānti? atha karṇadhāra evamāha - yatkhalu devo jānīyāt - siṃhaladvīpeṣu vāyavo vānti / atha tadyānapātramāruhya siṃhaladvīpaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: "In a former time, O son of good family, I was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> named King <s>Siṃhala</s> (Lion). Then I set out on a journey to <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> (the island of Lanka). Together with five hundred merchants' sons, loading abundant merchandise on carts, bundles, baskets, camels, oxen, donkeys, and other animals, I set out for <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>. Gradually, wandering through villages, cities, market towns, and trading posts, I reached <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>, where a fine vessel was procured. Then my helmsmen said: 'Tell us, tell us — to which islands do the winds blow for your journey? Do the winds blow to the jewel islands, or do the winds blow to the <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon) islands?' The helmsman then said: 'May the lord know — the winds blow to <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>.' Then, boarding that vessel, I set out for <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>."

children.text: tato 'haṃ siṃhaladvīpanivāsinībhī rākṣasībhiḥ saṃprasthito viditvā akālavāyava utsṛṣṭāḥ / tacca tadyānapātraṃ khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ viśīrṇam / te ca vaṇikpuruṣā udake patitā bāhubalena saṃtartumārabdhāḥ / tatastīrasya samīpamanuprāptāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Then, knowing that I had set out, the <s>Rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses) dwelling in <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> released untimely winds. That vessel was shattered to pieces. The merchant men, having fallen into the water, began to swim by the strength of their arms. Gradually they reached the vicinity of the shore."

children.text: tato rākṣasīnāṃ pañca śatāni niṣkrāntāni kilakilāyamānāni / kumārīrūpamabhinirmāya tadā kūlasya samīpamanuprāptāḥ / uttārya śāṭakāni dattvā udakebhya utkṣiptāḥ / te ca svakīyāni vastrāṇi śarīre lagnāni gṛhītvā niṣpīḍitumārabdhāḥ / niṣpīḍayitvā te tasmātsthānādatikramya anyapradeśe mahataścampakavṛkṣasya tale viśrāntāḥ / viśramitvā parasparaṃ sāṃkathyaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ - ko 'smākamupāyaḥ saṃvidyate? te kathayanti - nāsmākaṃ upāyasya sthānam / evaṃ sāṃkathyaṃ kṛtvā tūṣīṃbhāvena vyavasthitāḥ / atha teṣāṃ rākṣasyaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ purataḥ sthitvaivamāhuḥ - svāgatam / bhavanta āgacchatām, asvāmikānāṃ svāmī bhava / agatikānāṃ gatiko bhava / advīpānāṃ dvīpo bhava / anālayanānāṃ aparāyaṇānāṃ ālayo bhava, parāyaṇo bhava / imāni te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi yānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi kaṭakakeyūrāṇāṃ maulikuṇḍalānāṃ gṛhāṇi udyānaramaṇīyāni puṣkiriṇīramaṇīyāni saṃtiṣṭhanti / tābhī rākṣasībhirekaikaṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhītvā svakaṃ svakaṃ niveśanaṃ pratyudgatāḥ / yā ca tāsāṃ rākṣasīnāṃ vṛddhatarā, tayāhaṃ svakīyaṃ niveśanaṃ nītvā divyarasasāgropetenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ / saṃtarpayitvā krīḍitumārabdhā / sa tu tato mānuṣyakena saukhyena saṃtarpitaḥ / evaṃ dvitrisaptadinānyatikrāntāni / sa rātrau śayitaḥ / evaṃ yāvatpaśyati ratikarahasanaṃ tadāhaṃ vismayamāpannaḥ / na kadācitsyānmayā dṛṣṭaṃ vā śrutaṃ vā prajvalitameva ratikarahasanam, tadaiva mayā tasya pratyāhāraḥ kṛtaḥ - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tvaṃ hasase? iyaṃ siṃhaladvīpanivāsinī rākṣasī / sā tava jivitāntarāyaṃ kariṣyati / tadā me tasya pratyāhāraḥ kṛtaḥ - tvaṃ jānāsi rākṣasīti? sa kathayati - yadi na pratīyasi, dakṣiṇapanthalikāṃ gṛhītvā anuvicaran gaccha / tatrāyaṃ sa nagaramūrdhvamuccaṃ gavākṣatoraṇaviprahīṇaṃ cāpratihatam / tatrānekāni vaṇigjanāni bhakṣayitvā asthīniprakṣiptāni / anye ca jīvanto anye ca mṛtāḥ / yadi na pratīyasi, tadapi mārgaṃ gaccha / gatvā ca mārgaṃ nirīkṣasva, tadā me śraddhāsyasi / tadā tasyāstena mohajālā nāma nidrāti sā //
children.translated_text: "Then five hundred <s>Rākṣasīs</s> came forth, shrieking. Having magically assumed the form of young maidens, they then approached the vicinity of the bank. Having brought them out of the water, they gave them garments. The men, taking their own clothes that clung to their bodies, began to wring them out. After wringing them, they moved from that place and rested at the foot of a great <s>campaka</s> tree in another area. Having rested, they began to converse among themselves: 'What means of escape is available to us?' They said: 'We have no means of escape.' Having conversed thus, they remained in silence. Then those <s>Rākṣasīs</s>, standing before the men, spoke thus: 'Welcome! Come, O venerable ones! Be a master to the masterless! Be a way for those without a way! Be an island for those without an island! Be a shelter and a refuge for those without shelter or refuge! Here are your houses of food, houses of drink, houses of vehicles, houses of garments, houses of bracelets, armlets, crowns, and earrings, delightful gardens, and delightful lotus ponds.' Those <s>Rākṣasīs</s>, each taking one man, led them to their own respective dwellings. And the eldest among those <s>Rākṣasīs</s> took me to her own dwelling and satisfied me with food prepared with divine flavors. Having satisfied me, she began to make love. And he was gratified with that human pleasure. Thus two, three, seven days passed. He lay down at night. Then, seeing such laughing during lovemaking, I became filled with wonder. 'I have never before seen or heard of such blazing laughter during lovemaking!' Then I confronted her about it: 'Why do you laugh?' 'This one is a <s>Rākṣasī</s> dwelling in <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>! She will bring about the end of your life!' Then I confronted her: 'How do you know she is a <s>Rākṣasī</s>?' He said: 'If you do not believe, take the southern path and go searching along it. There, at the top of the city, is a high window-tower, unobstructed. There, having devoured many merchant-folk, their bones have been cast down. Some are living and others are dead. If you do not believe, go that way. Having gone, look at the road — then you will believe me.' Then her delusion-net named sleep overcame her."

children.text: Vaidya 286

atha sa bodhisattvo rātriprathamayāme samaye tasyā rākṣasyāḥ sakāśādutthāya saṃprasthitaḥ / candrāvabhāsaṃ khaṅgaṃ sajjīkṛtam / upagṛhyānuvicaraṃstāṃ dakṣiṇapanthalikāṃ gṛhītvā saṃprasthitaḥ / anupūrveṇāyasaṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ, samantena parikramati / na ca dvārāṇi gavākṣāṇi samanupaśyati / atha tasminnāyase nagare mahān yaścampakavṛkṣastatraivāruhya tato mayā teṣāmutkāsanaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ / tato me vaṇikpuruṣāḥ kathayanti - yatkhalu mahāsārthavāho jānīyāt - vayaṃ rākṣasībhirāyase nagare prakṣiptāḥ / tadā dine dine śataṃ puruṣāṇāṃ gṛhītvā bhakṣayanti / tān bhakṣayitvā asthīnyatraivāyase nagare kṣipanti / tena tasya bhūtapūrvaṃ varṇitam / tadāhaṃ campakavṛkṣādavatīrya punareva dakṣiṇāṃ panthalikāṃ gṛhītvā anuvicaran tvarita āgacchāmi sma / tato praviṣṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>bodhisattva</s>, rising from beside that <s>rākṣasī</s> (demoness) at the time of the first watch of the night, set out. He readied his moon-gleaming sword. Taking it up and proceeding along, he took the southern path and set out. Gradually he reached the iron city and walked around it on all sides. But he could not see any doors or windows. Then in that iron city there was a great <s>campaka</s> tree, and having climbed up it, I made a coughing sound to them. Then the merchant men told me: 'Let the great caravan leader know — we have been cast by the <s>rākṣasīs</s> into this iron city. Day after day they seize a hundred men and devour them. Having devoured them, they throw the bones right here in the iron city.' He described what had happened before. Then I, descending from the <s>campaka</s> tree and again taking the southern path, proceeded hurriedly and came back. Then I entered.

children.text: atha ratikaro māmetadavocat - dṛṣṭaste sārthavāha madvacanam? uktaṃ ca mayā - dṛṣṭaṃ yuṣmākaṃ satyaṃ sāṃkathyakṛtam / tadā me 'sya pratyāhāraḥ kṛtaḥ - satyameva, ka upāyo 'smākam? atha sa ratikara etadavocat - asti me mahāsārthavāhopāyam, yenopāyena siṃhaladvīpāt svastikṣemābhyāṃ jambūdvīpaṃ nirgacchasi / punareva jambudvīpamapasarasi / atha sa ratikaro māmetadavocat - asti tasminneva dvīpe mahāsamudratīre devabālāho nāmāśvarājo hīnadīnānukampakaḥ / sa ca bālāho 'śvarājaḥ / sarvaśvetānāmauṣadhīṃ bhuktvā suvarṇavālukāsthale āvartanaparivartanasaṃparivartanaṃ kṛtvā śarīraṃ pracchoḍayati, pracchoḍayitvā pratyāhāraṃ kurute - kaḥ pāragāmī, kaḥ pāragāmī kaḥ pāragāmīti? tvayaivaṃ vaktavyam - ahaṃ deva pāragāmīti / evaṃ sāṃkathyaṃ kṛtvā sā rākṣasī samīpamupagamya sārdhaṃ śayita eva prativibuddhā / sā kathayati - āryaputra, kathaṃ te śarīraṃ śītalam? tadā mayā tasyā mṛṣāvādaṃ pratyāhāraṃ kṛtam / bahirnagarasya uccāraprasraveṇa niṣkrānto 'ham, tataḥ śarīraṃ śītalam / ityuktvā sā punarapi śayitā / tataḥ prātaḥ sūryasya cābhyudgamanakālasamaye utthāya teṣāṃ vaṇikpurūṣāṇāmārocayati sma - āgacchantu bhavanto bahirnagarasya gacchāmaḥ / te sarve sahitāḥ samagrā bahirnagarasya saṃprasthitāḥ / te ca bahirnagarasya gatvā ekānte viśrāntāḥ sāṃkathyaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ - kasya kīdṛśī bhāryā snehavatī? kecitkathayanti - atisnehaṃ na kurute / kecitkathayanti - mama divyarasarasāgropetairāhāraiḥ saṃdhārayati / kecit kathayanti - nānāvidhairvastrairmama saṃdhārayati / kecitkathayanti - mama divyamaulīkuṇḍalasragdāmāni dhārayati / kecitkathayanti - nāsmākaṃ kāyadaurbalyam / kecitkathayanti - mama vividhāni candanakarpūrakastūrikādīni dhārayati / evaṃ taiḥ sāṃkathyaṃ kṛtam / tadā teṣāṃ vaṇikpuruṣāṇāṃ pratyāhāraṃ karoti sma - na yuṣmākaṃ yuktamidaṃ yadvayaṃ rākṣasībhiḥ prasaktāḥ / iti śrutvā te vihvalībhūtāḥ evamāhuḥ - satyaṃ mahāsārthavāha, rākṣasī siṃhaladvīpanivāsinīti / tadā teṣāṃ mayā pratyāhāraḥ kṛtaḥ - satyaṃ satyaṃ buddhadharmasaṃghebhyaṃ, neyaṃ mānuṣī, rākṣasī / atha te vaṇikpuruṣāḥ kathayanti - kāsmākaṃ gatiḥ? kiṃ parāyaṇam? tadā teṣāṃ mayā pratyāhāraḥ kṛtaḥ - asmākaṃ gatiḥ śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇam? children.text: ) vaṇikpurūṣāḥ kathayanti - upadarśaya sārthavāha / atha sa teṣāmevamāha - asti yuṣmākaṃ siṃhaladvīpe bālāho nāma aśvarājaḥ / sa ca hīnadīnānukampakaḥ / sa sarvaśvetānāmauṣadhīrbhuktvā suvarṇavālukāsthale āvartanaṃ karoti / kṛtvā ca śarīraṃ pracchoḍayitvā vāṇīṃ pratyāharediti - kaḥ pāragāmī kaḥ pāragāmī kaḥ pāragāmīti / tatrāsmābhirgantavyam - vayaṃ pāraṃgāmina iti / atha te vaṇikpurūṣā ūcuḥ - katame dine gacchāmo vayam? sa pratyāhāraṃ kartumārabdhaḥ - tṛtīye divase 'vaśyaṃ gantavyam / puruṣeṇa saṃbalaṃ kartavyamiti / te kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā punareva tannagaraṃ praviṣṭāḥ svakasvakaṃ niveśanamupagatā / tābhī rākṣasībhiḥ saṃbhāṣitāḥ - śrāntastvam, dṛṣṭāste tānyudyānaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīśatāni ramaṇīyāni? sa kathayati - na ca te kiṃcid dṛṣṭam / atha sā rākṣasī tametadavocat - santi āryaputra vividhānyasmin siṃhaladvīpe udyānaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni vividhavicitrapuṣpaparipūrṇāni / anekāni ca puṣkariṇīśatāni ramaṇīyāni / sa pratyāhāraṃ kartumārabdhaḥ - tṛtīye divase gamiṣyāmītyataḥ saṃbalaṃ kartavyam / udyānabhūmidarśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi / tāni ca vividhāni puṣkariṇīśatāni ramaṇīyāni udyānaśatāni puṣpaparipūrṇāni paśyāmi / tāni ca vividhāni puṣpāṇi gṛhītvā āgamiṣyāmi / sā kathayati sma - āryaputra / evaṃ karomyaham / tatastena śarīramanuvicintya / (?) atha rākṣasyo jānanti yogaṃ tenāsmākaṃ (?) jīvitāntarāyaṃ kariṣyanti / īdṛśaṃ śarīramanuvicintya tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ / tasya tayā praṇītāpraṇītānyāhārāṇyanupradattā / bhuktvā ca ucchvāsaṃ choritam / sā kathayati rākṣasī - āryaputra kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ucchvāsaṃ choritam? atha sa tāmetadavocat - svadeśābhiratā jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ / sā āha - kiṃ karoṣyāryaputra svakīyena viṣayena? asminneva siṃhaladvīpe vividhānyannagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi vividhānyudyānaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni / vividhasukhamanubhavase / kiṃ jambudvīpamanuśocase? tadāhaṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ / sa taṃ divasamatikrāntaḥ / dvitīye divase praṇītānyāhārāṇi satvaramanupradattāni sajjīkṛtāni / tṛtīye divase pratyūṣakālasamaye sarve te saṃprasthitāḥ / te ca bahirnagarasya niṣkrāntāḥ / niṣkramitvā kriyākāraṃ kartumārabdhāḥ / na punaḥ kenacit punareva siṃhaladvīpo nirīkṣitavyaḥ / tvaritamasmābhirgantavyam / īdṛśaṃ kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā saṃprasthitāḥ tvaritaṃ tvaritameva laghu laghveva gacchanti / anupūrveṇa yatra sa bālāhako 'śvarājastatrānuprāptāḥ / yāvatpaśyanti bālāhamaśvarājam / taṃ sarvaśvetānāmauṣadhīmāsvādayati / āsvādayitvā suvarṇavālukāsthale āvartanaṃ karoti / kṛtvā ca śarīraṃ pracchoḍayati / yadā śarīraṃ pracchoḍayati tadā siṃhaladvīpaṃ calati sma / trīṇi vākyāni pratyāharati sma - kaḥ pāragāmī, kaḥ pāragāmī, kaḥ pāragāmīti? atha sa bālāho 'śvarājastānetadavocat - bho vaṇikpuruṣāḥ / yadā śarīraṃ pracchoḍayāmi, na tadā yuṣmākaṃ kenacitsiṃhaladvīpo nirīkṣitavyaḥ / na kenaciccakṣurvisphuritavyam / te tādṛśaṃ kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā...... / tadāhaṃ prathamataramārūḍhaḥ, (
children.translated_text: ) The merchant men said: 'Show us, caravan leader.' Then he said this to them: 'On your <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> there is a horse-king named <s>Bālāha</s>. He is compassionate toward the wretched and lowly. Having eaten all the white herbs, he rolls on the golden sandy ground. Having done so and having shaken his body, he utters this call: "Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over?" We must go there and say: "We wish to cross over."' Then those merchant men said: 'On what day shall we go?' He began to reply: 'On the third day we must certainly go. Each man must prepare provisions.' Having made this agreement, they entered that city again and went each to his own dwelling. Those <s>rākṣasīs</s> spoke to them: 'You are tired. Have you seen those delightful gardens and the hundreds of beautiful lotus ponds?' He said: 'I have not seen anything.' Then that <s>rākṣasī</s> said this to him: 'There are, noble husband, various delightful gardens on this <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>, beautiful lotus ponds filled with various and wonderful flowers. There are hundreds of beautiful lotus ponds.' He began to reply: 'On the third day I shall go, therefore provisions must be prepared. I shall go to see the garden grounds. I shall see those various hundreds of beautiful lotus ponds and gardens full of flowers. Having gathered those various flowers, I shall return.' She said: 'Noble husband, I shall do so.' Then, reflecting on the situation in his mind — 'If the <s>rākṣasīs</s> learn of our plan, they will endanger our lives' — reflecting thus, he remained silent. She provided him with choice and exquisite foods. Having eaten, he heaved a sigh. That <s>rākṣasī</s> said: 'Noble husband, why did you sigh?' Then he said this to her: 'The people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are fond of their homeland.' She said: 'What will you do, noble husband, with your own country? On this very <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> there are various food-houses, drink-houses, clothing-houses, various delightful gardens, and beautiful lotus ponds. You experience various pleasures. Why do you grieve for <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?' Then I remained silent. That day passed. On the second day, choice foods were quickly provided and prepared. On the third day, at the time just before dawn, they all set out. They went outside the city. Having gone out, they began to make an agreement: no one shall look back again at <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>; we must go quickly. Having made this agreement, they set out, going swiftly, swiftly, lightly, lightly. Gradually they reached the place where the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s> was. They saw the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>. He was tasting all the white herbs. Having tasted them, he rolled on the golden sandy ground. Having done so, he shook his body. When he shook his body, <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> trembled. He uttered three phrases: 'Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over?' Then the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s> said this to them: 'O merchant men, when I shake my body, none of you must look at <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>. No one must blink his eyes.' They made such an agreement...... Then I was the first to mount (

children.text: ) paścātpañcaśatāṇi vaṇigjanāḥ / yadā te ārūḍhāḥ tadā siṃhaladvīpanivāsinyo rākṣasyaḥ kilakilāyamānāḥ pṛṣṭhato dhāvanti sma rudantyaḥ karuṇakaruṇairvilāpaiḥ / tatastai rudacchabdaṃ śrutvā pratinivartya nirīkṣitumārabdham / tairnirīkṣyante / tadā te 'dhomukhā udake patanti sma / yadā te udake patitāḥ, tadā rākṣasya utkṣipya māṃsaṃ bhakṣayanti sma / tadāhamekākī jambūdvīpameva pratyudgataḥ / tadā tīrasya samīpe bālāhamaśvarājaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tatraiva prakrāntaḥ / tato 'haṃ saṃprasthitaḥ / svakīyaṃ niveśanamanupūrveṇānuprāptaḥ / tadā me mātāpitārau kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya roditumārabdhau / tato bāṣpeṇa paṭalāni visphuṭitāni / tato draṣṭumārabdhau / tato mātāpitṛbhyāṃ sārdhaṃ viśrāntaḥ / tena teṣāṃ sarvaṃ bhūtapūrvaṃ vṛttāntamākhyātam / tatastau mātāpitarau kathayataḥ sma - jīvaṃstu putra tvamanuprāptaḥ / nāsmākaṃ dravyeṇa kṛtyam / jarākāle yaṣṭibhūto 'ndhakāre mārgasyopadarśakaḥ, maraṇakāle piṇḍadātā, mṛtasya sanāthīkaraṇīyam / yathā śītalo vāto nāma putra āhlādakaraḥ / etadvacanaṃ mātāpitarau cākhyātam / īdṛśaṃ mayā sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin sārthavāhabodhisattvabhūtena duḥkhamanubhūtam //
children.translated_text: Behind them were five hundred merchants. When they had boarded, the <s>rākṣasīs</s> (female demons) dwelling on <s>Siṃhala</s> island came running after them, shrieking with pitiful and heart-rending lamentations, weeping. Then, hearing the sound of weeping, they turned back and began to look. They were gazing back. Then they fell face-down into the water. When they had fallen into the water,

Then <s>Ratikara</s> said this to me: 'Did you see, caravan leader, what I told you?' And I said: 'I have seen it; what you said was true.' Then I replied to him: 'It is indeed true, but what means do we have?' Then <s>Ratikara</s> said this: 'I have a means, O great caravan leader, by which means you may depart safely and securely from <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> (Sri Lanka) to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (India). You may return again to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.' Then <s>Ratikara</s> said this to me: 'On that very island, at the shore of the great ocean, there is a horse-king named <s>Devabālāha</s>, compassionate toward the wretched and lowly. That horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>, having eaten all the white herbs, rolls and turns and revolves on the golden sandy ground, shakes his body, and having shaken it, calls out: "Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over?" You must say thus: "I wish to cross over, O divine one."' Having made this agreement, that <s>rākṣasī</s>, having come near and lain down together with him, awoke. She said: 'Noble husband, why is your body cold?' Then I gave her a false reply: 'I went outside the city to relieve myself, therefore my body is cold.' Having said this, she went back to sleep. Then in the morning, at the time of sunrise, rising up, he informed those merchant men: 'Come, sirs, let us go outside the city.' They all went together outside the city. Having gone outside the city, they rested in a secluded place and began to converse: 'Whose wife is more affectionate?' Some said: 'She does not show excessive affection.' Some said: 'She sustains me with food prepared with divine flavors and essences.' Some said: 'She sustains me with various garments.' Some said: 'She wears divine diadems, earrings, and garlands for me.' Some said: 'We have no bodily weakness.' Some said: 'She provides me with various sandalwood, camphor, musk, and the like.' Thus they conversed. Then he replied to those merchant men: 'It is not fitting for you that we are attached to <s>rākṣasīs</s>!' Hearing this, they became agitated and said: 'Is it true, O great caravan leader, that the inhabitants of <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> are <s>rākṣasīs</s>?' Then I replied to them: 'Truly, truly, by the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, she is not human — she is a <s>rākṣasī</s>!' Then those merchant men said: 'What is our refuge? What is our recourse?' Then I replied to them: 'What is our refuge, our shelter, our recourse?' (

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin bālāhakaṃ tamaśvarājabhūtenāvalokiteśvareṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena tādṛśādahaṃ mṛtyubhayātparimokṣitaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin na śaknomyavalokiteśvarasya puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ gaṇayitum / alpamātramidaṃ sāṃkathyaṃ kṛtaṃ ekaikaromavivarasya //
children.translated_text: Just so, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, I was liberated from such fear of death by <s>Bālāhaka</s>, the Horse-King, who is none other than <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Just so, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, I am unable to calculate the accumulation of merit of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. This discourse covers only a small portion — that of a single hair-pore.

children.text: iti aśvarājavarṇanaṃ nāma prathamaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, called 'The Description of the Horse-King.'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇāviṣkambhin suvarṇaṃ nāma romavivaram / tatrānekānigandharvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti sma / tena ca saṃsārikena duḥkhena na bādhyante / parameṇa saukhyena saṃtarpitā bhavanti / divyāni vastūni prādurbhavanti / tatra na ca te rāgeṇa bādhyante / na ca mohena bādhyante / na ca dveṣeṇa bādhyante / na ca te āghātacittamutpādayanti / na ca teṣāṃ hiṃsācittamutpadyate / te satatasamitamāryāṣṭāṅgikamārgamupadarśitā bhavanti / satatakālaṃ dharmābhikāṅkṣiṇo bhavanti / tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin suvarṇanāmaromavivare avabhāsaṃ nāma cintāmaṇiratnam / yadā te gandharvā abhiprāyaṃ cintayanti, tadā teṣāmabhiprāyo 'nusidhyati / tadā suvarṇaromavivarādatikramya kṛṣṇo nāma romavivaraḥ / tatrānekāni ṛṣikoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti / kecidekābhijñāḥ, kecid dvayabhijñāḥ, kecit tryabhijñāḥ, keciccaturabhijñāḥ, kecitpañcābhijñāḥ, kecitṣaḍabhijñāḥ / tasmiṃśca romavivare rūpyamayī bhūmiḥ, kanakamayāḥ parvatāḥ, rūpyamayāḥ śṛṅgāḥ, padmarāgairupacitāḥ parvatāḥ, tādṛśāḥ saptasaptatiparvatāḥ / ekaikaparvate 'śītisahasrāṇi ṛṣīṇāṃ prativasanti / teṣāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāmīdṛśā parṇakuṭirakalpavṛkṣāṇi dṛśyante / lohitadaṇḍāḥ (
