children.text: ) suvarṇarūpyapatrā ratnāvabhāsitāḥ / ekaikapārśve romavivare catasraḥ puṣkariṇyaḥ / kecidaṣṭāṅgopetena vāriṇā paripūrṇāḥ kecitpuṣpaparipūrṇāḥ / tasminnupacārasamīpe divyā agurudrumavṛkṣāḥ, sugandhāścandanavṛkṣāḥ, pariśobhitāḥ kalpavṛkṣāḥ, saṃdṛśyante / divyālaṃkārapralambitā maulīkuṇḍalapralambitā hārārdhahārapralambitāḥ keyūranūpurasragdāmapralambitāḥ sauvarṇapatrāḥ / tatraikaikakalpavṛkṣe gandharvaśataṃ viśrāntam / yadā te vādyapratyāhāramudīrayanti, tadā mṛgapakṣyādayaḥ saṃvegamāpadyante - sukhaduḥkhamidaṃ sāṃsārikāṇāṃ sattvānām / kathaṃ jambudvīpe duḥkhamanubhavanti? jātijarāmaraṇaṃ paśyanti? iṣṭapriyaviyogamapriyasaṃprayogaṃ paśyanti? mānuṣyakāṇi bahūni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti? ityevaṃ te mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ saṃvegamanuvicintya yadā kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya nāmānusmaranti, tadā teṣāṃ divyarasarasāgropetā āhārāḥ prādurbhavanti / divyāni ca saugandhikāni vastūni prādurbhavanti / divyāni vastrāṇi prādurbhavanti / yadā te 'bhiprāyamanuvicintayanti, tadābhiprāyāḥ sidhyanti //
children.translated_text: With leaves of gold and silver, illuminated by jewels. On each side of the hair-pore are four lotus ponds — some filled with water endowed with the eight qualities, some filled with flowers. In the vicinity there are divine <s>aguru</s> (aloewood) trees, fragrant sandalwood trees, resplendent wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣas</s>) to be seen, adorned with divine ornaments hanging down, with diadems and earrings hanging,

Just so, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, there is a hair-pore called <s>Suvarṇa</s> (Golden). In it dwell many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians). They are not afflicted by <s>saṃsāric</s> (worldly) suffering. They are nourished with supreme happiness. Divine objects manifest there. There they are not afflicted by desire, nor are they afflicted by delusion.

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - paramāścaryādbhutaprāpto 'haṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kulaputra paramavismayamāpannaḥ? atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - yadā bhagavan kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtraratnarājasya nāmānusmaranti, tadābhiprāyā anusidhyanti / yasya nāmadheyamātreṇa īdṛśāni vastūni prādurbhavanti, sukhitāste sattvā ye kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ śroṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, yoniśaṃ ca manasi kariṣyanti / ye kāraṇḍavyūhasya mahāyānasūtrarājasyaikākṣaramapi likhāpayiṣyanti, te idaṃ sāṃsārikaṃ duḥkhaṃ na paśyanti / na ca te caṇḍālakukkurakuleṣu jāyante / na ca te hīnendriyā bhavanti / na ca te khañjakubjakordhvanāsagaṇḍalamboṣṭhāśca sattvāḥ kuṣṭhinaśca santaḥ / na ca teṣāṃ kāye vyādhiḥ saṃkramate / ārogyabalavatprīṇitendriyāśca bhavanti / atha bhagavān sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, yastvamīdṛśaṃ pratibhānaṃ karoṣi / anekāni devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyā upāsakopāsikāsahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni - tvayedṛśaṃ dharmasāṃkathyaṃ kṛtam / yatastvayedṛśo vaipulyapratibhānaḥ kṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'I have attained the utmost wonder and amazement, O Blessed One!' The Blessed One said: 'For what reason, O son of good family, have you reached such supreme astonishment?' Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'When, O Blessed One, beings remember the name of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, then their aspirations are fulfilled.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - yadā bhagavannidaṃ praśnamanirdiṣṭaṃ tadā devaputrāṇāmabhedyā śraddhotpannā / atha bhagavān sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamevaṃ punaḥ punastathāgatamadhyeṣase / tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin kṛṣṇānnāma romavivarādavatīrya ratnakuṇḍalo nāma romavivaraḥ / tatrānekāni gandharvakanyākoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti / tāśca gandharvakanyā abhirūpāḥ darśanīyāḥ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā divyālaṃkāravibhūṣitaśarīrā apsarasāmiva pratispardhinyaḥ tādṛśyaḥ, paramaśobhanāḥ / na ca tā rāgaduḥkhena bādhyante / na ca dveṣaduḥkhena bādhyante / na ca mohaduḥkhena bādhyante / na ca tāsāṃ kāye kiṃcinmānuṣīduḥkhaṃ saṃvidyate / tāśca gandharvakanyāstrikālamavalokiteśvarasya (

children.text: ) bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmamanusmaranti / yadā trikālamanusmaranti, tadā tāsāṃ sarvavastūni prādurbhavanti //
children.translated_text: of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> remember his name. When they remember it at the three times of day, then all objects manifest for them.

Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'When, O Blessed One, this question was being expounded, unshakable faith arose in the <s>devaputras</s> (sons of the gods).' Then the Blessed One gave his approval: 'Well said, well said, O son of good family, that you thus repeatedly beseech the <s>Tathāgata</s>!' 'Just so, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, descending from the hair-pore called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (Dark),

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇāviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - gamiṣyāmyahaṃ bhagavan / tāni romavivarāṇi draṣṭukāmo 'ham / bhagavānāha - agrāhyāste kulaputra romavivarā asaṃsparśāḥ / yathā ākāśadhāturagrāhyo 'saṃsparśaḥ, evameva te kulaputra romavivarā agrāhyā asaṃsparśāḥ / teṣu romavivareṣu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvasteṣāṃ romavivarāṇāṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi paribhramitaḥ, na ca tena tāni romavivarāṇi dṛṣṭāṇi / yasyaikaikaromavivare sthitaṃ buddhaśatam, tenāpi na dṛṣṭāṇi, prāgevānye bodhisattvabhūtāḥ //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I wish to go, Blessed One. I desire to see those hair-pores.' The Blessed One said: 'Those hair-pores, O son of good family, are ungraspable and intangible. Just as the realm of space is ungraspable and intangible, even so, O son of good family, those hair-pores are ungraspable and intangible. In those hair-pores, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, wandered for twelve years, yet he did not see those hair-pores. In each single hair-pore dwells a hundred <s>Buddhas</s>, yet even he did not see them — how much less other <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - yadā bhagavan samantabhadreṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na dṛṣṭaṃ dvādaśavarṣāṇi paribhramatā, na ca tena tāni romavivarāṇi dṛṣṭāni, asyaikaikaromavivare sthitaṃ buddhaśataṃ tenāpi na dṛṣṭam, tadā teṣāṃ romavivarāṇāmantato 'hamapi kiṃ gamiṣyāmi? āha - kulaputra, mayāpi tasya romavivaraṃ vīkṣamāṇena parimārgayamāṇena na dṛśyate / sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin kulaputra, ayaṃ māyāvī asādhyaḥ sūkṣma evamanudṛśyate / nirañjano rūpī mahāpī(?) śatasahasrabhujaḥ koṭiśatasahasranetro viśvarūpī ekādaśaśīrṣaḥ mahāyogī nirvāṇabhūmivyavasthitaḥ sucetano mahāprājñaḥ bhavottārakaḥ kulīno 'nādarśī prājño nirdeśastathācchāyābhūtaḥ sarvadharmeṣu, evameva kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo na śruto na kenacid dṛśyate / tasya svabhāvakā anyathārtagatā na paśyanti, prāgeva samantabhadrādayo 'nye ca bodhisattvāḥ / acintyo 'yaṃ kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prātihāryāṇi samupadarśayati / anekāni ca bodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi paripācayati, sattvāṃśca tān bodhimārge pratiṣṭhāpayati / pratiṣṭhāpayitvā sukhāvatīlokadhātumanugacchati / amitābhasya tathāgatasyāntike dharmamanuśṛṇoti //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'When, Blessed One, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, wandering for twelve years did not see them, and those hair-pores were not seen by him, and the hundred <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in each single hair-pore were not seen even by him — then what purpose would it serve for me to go to those hair-pores?' He said: 'O son of good family, even I, looking and searching for his hair-pore, cannot see it. O son of good family <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, this one is a magician, unfathomable, subtle, and thus imperceptible. He is stainless, embodied, great, with a hundred thousand arms, with tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of eyes, of universal form, eleven-headed, a great <s>yogī</s>, established on the ground of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, mindful, of great wisdom, a deliverer from existence, noble, impartial, wise — his teaching is like a shadow upon all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, O son of good family, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, is neither heard of nor seen by anyone. Those of a different nature and understanding do not perceive his true nature — how much less <s>Samantabhadra</s> and other <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Inconceivable, O son of good family, is this <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, who displays miracles. He ripens many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and establishes beings on the path of enlightenment. Having established them, he sends them to the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-realm. In the presence of <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, he hears the <s>Dharma</s>.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - kenopāyena bhagavan paśyāmi ahamavalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam? bhagavānāha - yadi kulaputra ihaiva sahālokadhātumāgacchati mama darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya / atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - anujānāmyahaṃ bhagavan, avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva āgacchati? bhagavānāha - yadā kulaputra sattvaparipāko bhavati, tadāvalokiteśvaraḥ prathamataramāgacchati //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'By what means, Blessed One, may I see <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'If, O son of good family, he comes here to this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm for seeing me, for worshipping me, for attending upon me.' Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'May I know, Blessed One — is <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, coming?' The Blessed One said: 'When, O son of good family, the ripening of beings occurs, then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> comes first of all.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bodhisattvaḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ - kiṃ mayā pāparatena cirakālajīvikayā tenāvalokiteśvaradarśanaviprahīṇenāndhabhūtena tamonuprāptamārgasaṃprasthitena? atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bodhisattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - katamasmin kāle bhagavannavalokiteśvara āgacchati? atha bhagavānapīdaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā hasati, vyavahasati ca - akālaste kulaputra avalokiteśvarasyāgamanakālasamayaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra tato romavivarādavatīrya amṛtabindurnāma romavivaraḥ, tatrānekāni devaputra koṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi (

children.translated_text: dwell. Some are established on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), some on the second <s>bhūmi</s>, some on the third, some on the fourth, some on the fifth, some on the sixth, some on the seventh, some on the eighth, some on the ninth, and some <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> established on the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> dwell there. Just as, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, in this hair-pore called <s>Amṛtabindu</s> there are sixty mountains made of gold and silver. Each mountain is sixty thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height. Those mountains have ninety-nine thousand peaks adorned with divine gold and jewels. On their slopes dwell some <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have generated the first thought of enlightenment. In those mountain ranges dwell many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), who in that hair-pore continuously sustain the radiance of the sun. Just as, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, in that hair-pore called <s>Amṛtabindu</s> there are many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of celestial palaces, adorned with jewels, beautiful, splendid, and wonderful, with hundreds of thousands of pearl necklaces hanging down. In those palaces, <s>bodhisattvas</s> rest and engage in <s>Dharma</s> discussion. Then, departing from those palaces, they go forth to their respective walking places. In each walking place there are seventy lotus ponds — some filled with water possessing the eight qualities, some filled with various flowers: <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>saugandhika</s>, <s>māndārava</s>, and <s>mahāmāndārava</s> flowers. In those walking places there are delightful <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees), red-stemmed, with gold and silver leaves, hung with divine ornaments, hung with crest-jewels, earrings, garlands and wreaths, hung with necklaces and half-necklaces, hung with armlets. Others are hung with various ornaments. In those walking places, at night the <s>bodhisattvas</s> walk and reflect on the various <s>Mahāyāna</s> teachings, contemplate the ground of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, contemplate the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, think on the escape from hell, and having reflected, cultivate <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). Thus, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, in that hair-pore such <s>bodhisattvas</s> dwell. Then, descending from the hair-pore called <s>Amṛtavittabindu</s>, there is a hair-pore called <s>Vajramukha</s> (Diamond-faced), where many hundreds of thousands of <s>kinnaras</s> dwell. They appear supremely beautiful with armlets, earrings, bracelets, various garlands, ornaments, and unguents. Constantly devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>, dwelling single-mindedly in <s>Dharma</s> and <s>maitrī</s>, endowed with patience, contemplating <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and possessed of a sense of urgency regarding human existence. Such, O son of good family, are those <s>kinnaras</s>, delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>. In that very hair-pore there are many hundreds of thousands of mountain caverns — some made of diamond, some of ruby, some of sapphire, some of the seven jewels. Such signs of the true <s>Dharma</s> are seen in that hair-pore, O son of good family. In that hair-pore there are many <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s>, many coral trees, <s>candana</s> trees, fragrant trees, many hundreds of thousands of lotus ponds, divine palaces, supremely beautiful and delightful mansions made of crystal and silver. Where such palaces appear, in those palaces the <s>kinnaras</s> rest. Having rested, they engage in <s>Dharma</s> discussion — they discuss the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), they discuss the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), they discuss the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). Having thus discussed the six perfections (<s>ṣaṭpāramitā</s>), they walk in their respective walking places. Some walking places are made of gold. In those walking places, nearby, there are <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> with red stems and gold and silver leaves, hung with divine ornaments, hung with crest-jewels, earrings, garlands and wreaths, hung with necklaces and half-necklaces, hung with jeweled necklaces. children.text: ) teṣu caṃkrameṣu kinnarāścaṃkramanti / caṃkramyamāṇāḥ sāṃsārikaṃ satyamanuvicintayanti - aho duḥkham / jātirduḥkham / aho duḥkham / jarāmaraṇaduḥkham / aho duḥkham / tadapi dāridryaduḥkham / iṣṭapriyaviyogāpriyāviyogaduḥkham / tadapi kaṣṭataraṃ duḥkham / ye cāvīcāvupapannā rauravopapannāḥ, kālasūtropapannāḥ, hāhave mahānarake upapannāḥ, pratāpane narake upapannāḥ, agnighaṭeṣupapannāḥ, vajraśaileṣupapannāḥ, pretanagaropapannāḥ, tadeṣāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ duḥkhataram / evaṃ ca te kinnarāścittena cintayanti / cintayitvā nairvāṇikīṃ bhūmīṃ cintayanti / evameva kulaputra kinnarā dharmābhiratāḥ satatakālamavalokiteśvarasya nāmanusmaranti / yadā te nāmānusmaranti, tadā teṣāṃ sarvopakaraṇairupasthitā bhavanti / evaṃ durlabhaḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ mātāpitṛbhūtaḥ sarvasattveṣvabhayaṃdadaḥ / sarvasattveṣu mārgopadarśakaḥ / sarvasattveṣu kalyāṇamitraḥ / evaṃ kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ / durlabhaṃ kulaputra tasya nāmagrahaṇam / ye ca tasya ṣaḍakṣarīmahāvidyānāmānusmaranti, tadā teṣu romavivareṣu jāyante / na ca punareva saṃsāre saṃsaranti / romavivarādromavivaramupasaṃkrāmanti / teṣāṃ teṣu romavivareṣu tāvattiṣṭhanti yāvannairvāṇikīṃ bhūmimanveṣante //
children.translated_text: ) On those walking paths, <s>Kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians) walk about. While walking, they contemplate the truth of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence): 'Alas, suffering! Birth is suffering! Alas, suffering! Old age and death are suffering! Alas, suffering! And poverty is suffering! Separation from what is loved and dear, and union with what is unloved — that too is the most grievous suffering! Those who are born in <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell), born in <s>Raurava</s> (the Screaming hell), born in <s>Kālasūtra</s> (the Black Thread hell), born in the great hell of <s>Hāhava</s>, born in <s>Pratāpana</s> (the Scorching hell), born in the fire-pots, born on the vajra mountains, born in the city of <s>Pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) — for all those beings it is the most intense suffering.' Thus those <s>Kinnaras</s> reflect in their minds. Having reflected, they contemplate the ground of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Just so, O son of good family, the <s>Kinnaras</s>, delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>, constantly remember the name of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. When they remember his name, then all provisions appear before them. So rare, O son of good family, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, who is like a mother and father to all beings, who gives fearlessness to all beings, who shows the path to all beings, who is a spiritual friend to all beings. Such, O son of good family, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. Rare, O son of good family, is the taking of his name. Those who remember the name of the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s> (Great Six-Syllable Spell) are born in his body-hair pores. They no longer wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>. They pass from body-hair pore to body-hair pore. They remain in those body-hair pores until they find the ground of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, resting his cheek on his hand, stood absorbed in thought: 'What is the use of my long life, devoted to evil, deprived of the sight of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, become blind, having set out on a path reached by darkness?' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> again spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'At what time, Blessed One, does <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> come?' Then the Blessed One, having heard these words, laughed and said: 'The time of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>'s coming is untimely for you, O son of good family. Just as, O son of good family, having descended from that hair-pore, there is a hair-pore called <s>Amṛtabindu</s> (Drop of Nectar), where many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s>

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkabhī bhagavantametadavocat - kuto bhagavan ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā prāpyate? bhagavānāha - durlabhā kulaputra sā ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā / na ca tathāgatā jānanti prāgeva bodhisattvabhūtāḥ / atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - yadbhagavan tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā na jānanti? bhagavānāha - kulaputra sā ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā tvavalokiteśvarasya paramahṛdayam / yaśca paramahṛdayaṃ jānāti sa mokṣaṃ jānāti / atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - asti bhagavan kecitsattvā ye ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ jānanti? bhagavānāha - na kaścijjānīte kulaputra / ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā rājñī / eṣā durāsadā aprameyā yoginastathāgatā jānanti prāgeva bodhisattvabhūtāḥ / asyāḥ kulaputra ṣaḍakṣarīmahāvidyāyāḥ kāraṇena sarve tathāgatāḥ ṣoḍaśakalyāṇasaṃkhyeyāḥ paribhramitāḥ prāgeva bodhisattvabhūtāḥ kuto jānanti? ayaṃ sa paramahṛdayaḥ avalokiteśvarasya / yo 'pyayaṃ paribhramati jaganmaṇḍale, kaścijjānīte ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyām / puṇyavantaste sattvā ye ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ satataparigrahaṃ japābhiyuktā bhavanti / tasyā japakāle tu navanavatigaṅgānadīvālukopamāstathāgatāḥ saṃnipatanti, paramāṇurajopamā bodhisattvāḥ saṃnipatanti, ṣaṭpāramitā dvārasthā bhavanti / anye ca dvātriṃśaddevanikāyāḥ devaputrāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ / cattvāraśca mahārājānaścatasro diśo rakṣanti / sāgaraśca nāgarājaḥ / anavataptaśca nāgarājaḥ / takṣakaśca nāgarājaḥ / vāsukirnāgarājaḥ - evaṃpramukhānyanekāni nāgarājakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi dharaṇīṃ parirakṣanti / anye ca bhaumā yakṣāḥ / anye cāvakāśaṃ rakṣanti / tasya kulaputrasya ekaikaromavivare (
Vaidya 293
children.translated_text: [Vaidya edition, page 293]

children.text: ) tathāgatakoṭyo viśramanti, viśramitvā sādhukāramanuprayanti - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvamīdṛśaṃ cintāmaṇiratnalabdhalābho 'si / vimokṣitāste saptakulavaṃśā jātiparaṃparayā / ye ca tava kulaputra kukṣigatāḥ prāṇinaḥ, sarve te 'vaivartikā bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti / yaḥ kaścidimāṃ dhārayet ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ kāyagatāṃ kaṇṭhagatāṃ vā, sa kulaputra vajrakāyaśarīra iti veditavyaḥ, dhātustūpa iti veditavyaḥ, tathāgatajñānakoṭiriti veditavyaḥ / yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ japanti so 'kṣayapratibhāno bhavati / jñānarāśiviśuddho bhavati / mahākaruṇayā samanvāgato bhavati / sa dine dine ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayati / vidyādharacakravartyabhiṣekaṃ pratilabhate / yasya kasyaciducchavasyocchvāsapraśvāsaṃ dadāti maitryā vā dveṣeṇa vā, sarve te 'vaivartikādhisattvā bhavanti, kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante / ye kecidvastrasparśanenāpi spṛśanti, sarve te caramabhavikā bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ / darśanamātreṇa strī vā puruṣo vā dārikā vā mṛgapakṣiṇo gomahiṣagardabhādayaśca cakṣurdarśanenāpi paśyanti, sarve te caramabhavikā bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ, jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaduḥkhapriyaviprayogavihīṇā bhaveyuḥ / acintyā yoginaśca bhaveyuḥ / evaṃ tu ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ japamānasya saṃcodano bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) millions of <s>Tathāgatas</s> rest, and having rested, they utter their approval: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family, that you have obtained such a wish-fulfilling jewel! Your seven generations of family lineage are liberated. Whatever living beings are within your womb, all of them shall become non-retrogressing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Whoever holds this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s> on their body or at their throat, that son of good family should be known as having a vajra body, should be known as a relic <s>stūpa</s>, should be known as a summit of <s>Tathāgata</s> wisdom. Whatever son or daughter of good family recites this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>, they become inexhaustible in eloquence, purified in the mass of wisdom, endowed with great compassion. Day by day they fulfill the six <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections). They obtain the consecration of a <s>Vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder) <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign). Whoever gives breath to any breathing being, whether through loving-kindness or through aversion, all of them become non-retrogressing <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and swiftly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. Whoever touches them even by the touch of a garment, all of them shall become <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in their final existence. By the mere sight of them — whether woman or man, girl, deer, birds, cows, buffalo, donkeys, or others — whoever sees them even with their eyes, all of them shall become <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in their final existence, free from the suffering of birth, old age, disease, death, and separation from the beloved. And they shall become inconceivable yogins. Such is the encouragement for one who recites the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>.'"

Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "From where, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, can the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s> (Great Six-Syllable Spell) be obtained?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Difficult to obtain, O son of good family, is that <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>. Not even the <s>Tathāgatas</s> know it, let alone those who are still <s>Bodhisattvas</s>." Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones not know it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "O son of good family, that <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s> is the supreme heart-essence of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. One who knows the supreme heart-essence knows liberation." Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Are there, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, any beings who know the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "No one knows it, O son of good family. The <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s> is a queen. She is unapproachable, immeasurable. The yogin <s>Tathāgatas</s> know her, let alone those who are still <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Because of this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>, O son of good family, all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have wandered through sixteen incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) — how then could those who are still <s>Bodhisattvas</s> know it? This is the supreme heart-essence of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. Whoever wanders in the circle of the world, some may know the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>. Meritorious are those beings who constantly recite and are devoted to the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>. At the time of its recitation, <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal in number to the grains of sand of ninety-nine Ganges rivers assemble, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to atoms of dust assemble, the six <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections) stand at the door, and the thirty-two classes of <s>Devaputras</s> (divine sons) assemble. The four great kings protect the four directions. <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s> (serpent king), <s>Anavatapta</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s> — led by these, many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Nāgarājas</s> protect the earth. Other earthly <s>Yakṣas</s> protect the open sky. In each body-hair pore of that son of good family (

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan labheyamahaṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyām? so 'cintyo yogānāṃ cāprameyadhyānānāṃ ca aparisthitaścānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, nirvāṇasyopadarśakaḥ, mokṣasya praveśanam, rāgadveṣasya vyupaśamanam, dharmarājasya ca paripūraṇam, unmūlanaṃ ca saṃsārasya pañcagatikasya, saṃśoṣaṇaṃ ca nārakāṇāṃ kleśānām, samuddhātanamuttāraṇaṃ ca tiryagyonigatānām, āsvādo dharmāṇāṃ ca paripūraṇam, sarvajñajñānasya akṣayaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrotumicchāmi / bhagavan yo me ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāmanuprayacchati, tasya caturdvīpān saptaratnaparipūrṇānniryātayitum / yadi bhagavan likhyamānāyāpi bhūrjaṃ na saṃvidyate, na masiḥ, na ca karamam / madīyena śoṇitena masiṃ kuryāt, carmamutpāṭya bhūrjaṃ kuryāt, asthiṃ bhaṅktavā ca karamaṃ kuryāt, tadāpi bhagavan mama nāsti khedaṃ śarīrasya / sa ca me mātāpitṛbhūto bhavet gurūṇāmapi guruśca //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, may I obtain the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>? That inconceivable yoga and immeasurable <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), that which is unestablished in unsurpassed perfect awakening, that which shows <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, that which is the entrance to liberation, that which pacifies desire and aversion, that which fulfills the king of <s>Dharma</s>, that which uproots <s>saṃsāra</s> of the five destinies, that which dries up the afflictions of the hells, that which rescues and delivers those born in animal realms, that which is the relishing and fulfillment of all <s>Dharmas</s> — I wish to hear the inexhaustible teaching of omniscient wisdom! O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to whoever grants me the <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>, I would offer the four continents filled with the seven treasures. If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when it is to be written, there is no birch-bark, no ink, no pen — I would make ink from my own blood, tear off my skin to make birch-bark, break my bones to make a pen. Even then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I would have no weariness of body. And that one would be to me like a mother and father, a teacher even of teachers."

children.text: atha bhagavān sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhiṇaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - smarāmyahaṃ kulaputra asyāḥ ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyāḥ kāraṇena paramāṇurajopamān lokadhātūn paribhramitaḥ / anekāni tathāgatakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi mayā paryupāsitāni / na ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ sakāśātsacālaṃbāpi (?) śrutā / tadā ratnottamo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / tasya mayā purastādaśrūṇi pramuktāni / tadā tena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhenābhihitam - mā kulaputra evaṃ karuṇakarūṇānyaśrūṇi pramuñca / gaccha kulaputra yena padmottamo nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatra padmottamo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / sa imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ (
Vaidya 294
children.translated_text: [Vaidya edition, page 294]

children.text: ) mahāvidyāmanujānāti / tasya kulaputra ahaṃ ratnottamasya tathāgatasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ / yena padmottamasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā purastātprāñjalībhūtvottam - labheyamahaṃ bhagavan padmottama ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ rājñīṃ yasyā nāmānusmaraṇamātreṇa sarvapāpāni kṣayante, durlabhāṃ bodhiṃ pratilabhate, yenārthenāhaṃ kliṣṭo 'nekāni lokadhātūni / ihaivāgatvā mā vyarthaśramo bhaveyam / tadā padmottamastathāgata imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāguṇāṃ saṃsmārayati sma - tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra śakyate paramāṇurajaḥpramāṇamudgṛhītum, na tu kulaputra śakyate ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyā ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / śakyate mayā kulaputra catuḥsamudrasyaikaikāṃ vālukāṃ gaṇayitum, na tu kulaputra śakyate mayā ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyā ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra kaścideva puruṣo bhavet / sa gṛhaṃ pūrṇaṃ yojanasahasraṃ kuryāt dviguṇaṃ pañcayojanaśatāni / taṃ tilaphalaiḥ paripūrṇaṃ kuryāt / yatra sūcīvivaraṃ na saṃvidyate, tatra puruṣo dvāre sthāpito 'jarāmaraḥ / sa kalpaśatasyātikrāntasya asyaikatilaphalaṃ bahirdvāre prakṣipet / tadanena paryāyeṇa taṃ gṛhasamūhapratiṣṭhitāstilāḥ parikṣayaparyavadānaṃ yāvatkālena vrajeyuḥ, tacchakyate mayā gaṇayitum / na tu kulaputra śakyate ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyāḥ ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra caturdvīpe nānāvidhāni kṛṣiṃ kārayanti yavagodhūmaśālimudgamāṣādayastilakolakulatthādibhiḥ, tatra kālena kālaṃ nāgarājāno varṣadhārāmanuprayacchanti / tāni śasyāni niṣpādyante, tataste paripakkāḥ parichidyante / evaṃ jambudvīpaṃ khalaṃ kuryāt, tataste śakaṭairbhārairmuṭaiḥ piṭhakairgobhirgardabhādibhirlaṅghayitvā tasmin khalābhyantare prakṣiperan, tāni gobhirgardabhairmardayitvā mahāntaṃ rāśiṃ niṣpādyate / śakyate mayā kulaputra ekaikāni phalāni gaṇayitum, na tu kulaputra śakyate mayā ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyā ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra imā mahānadyo jambudvīpe pravahanti rātrau divā ca / tadyathā gaṅgā sītā yamunā sindhuḥ śatadruḥ candrabhāgā erāvatī sumāgandhā himaratī kalaśodarī ceti / ekaikanadī pañcasahasraparivārā / rātrau ca divā ca mahāsamudre pravahanti / evameva ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyā ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaḥ pravahati / tatrāsāṃ mahānadīnāṃ śakyate mayā ekaikabinduṃ gaṇayitum / na ca kulaputra śakyate mayā ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyā ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra caturdvīpeṣu catuṣpājjātīnāṃ gogardabhamahiṣāśvahastinaḥ, śvajambukacchāgalapaśavaḥ, tathā siṃhavyāghratarakṣumṛgamarkaṭaśaśakādayaḥ, eṣāṃ mayaikaikāni romāṇi śakyate gaṇayitum, na tu kulaputra ṣaḍākṣarimahāvidyāyāḥ śakyate ekajāpasya puṇyaskandhaṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra vajrāṅkuśo nāma parvatarājo navanavatiyojanasahasrāṇyucchrayeṇa caturaśītiyojanasahasrāṇyadhastāt / tasya parvatarājasya vajrāṅkuśasyaikaṃ pārśvaṃ caturaśītiyojanasahasram / tasya ca pārśve parvatarājasya jarāmaraḥ puruṣo bhavet / sa (
children.translated_text: grants the <s>mahāvidyā</s> (great spell). From him, O son of good family, I departed from the presence of <s>Ratnottama</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> and approached the buddha-field of <s>Padmottama</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, I bowed my head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood before him with palms joined, saying: 'May I obtain, O Blessed One <s>Padmottama</s>, the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> (six-syllable great spell), the queen, by the mere recollection of whose name all sins are destroyed and the hard-to-attain <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) is obtained — for the sake of which I have suffered through countless world-systems. Having come here, may my effort not be in vain.' Then <s>Padmottama</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> recalled the virtues of this <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>: 'Just as, O son of good family, it is possible to take the measure of atomic particles of dust, it is not possible, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. I am able, O son of good family, to count each grain of sand in the four oceans, but I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Suppose, O son of good family, there were a certain man. He would build a house a thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in extent, doubled to five hundred <s>yojanas</s>. He would fill it completely with sesame seeds, so that not even a needle's opening could be found. An ageless, immortal man is placed at the door. After the passing of a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), he would cast out a single sesame seed through the outer door. By this method, in the time it would take for the sesame seeds established in that collection of houses to reach complete exhaustion — that I am able to reckon. But I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Just as, O son of good family, in the four continents they cultivate various crops — barley, wheat, rice, mung beans, black beans, sesame, jujube, horse gram, and the like — and from time to time the <s>Nāgarājas</s> (serpent kings) provide showers of rain; those crops ripen and when fully grown are harvested. If one were to make <s>Jambudvīpa</s> into a threshing floor, and they would bring them by carts, by loads, by bundles, by baskets, by oxen and donkeys, and cast them into that threshing floor, and crush them with oxen and donkeys to produce a great heap — I am able, O son of good family, to count each individual grain, but I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Just as, O son of good family, these great rivers flow in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> by night and by day — namely, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Śatadru</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, <s>Erāvatī</s>, <s>Sumāgandhā</s>, <s>Himaratī</s>, and <s>Kalaśodarī</s> — each river attended by five thousand tributaries, flowing by night and by day into the great ocean — even so does the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> flow. Of those great rivers, I am able to count each individual drop, but I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Just as, O son of good family, among the four-footed creatures dwelling in the four continents — cows, donkeys, buffaloes, horses, elephants, dogs, jackals, goats, sheep, and also lions, tigers, leopards, deer, monkeys, hares, and others — I am able to count each individual hair of theirs, but I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Just as, O son of good family, there is a mountain king called <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>, ninety-nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height and eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> extending below. children.translated_text: once per passing <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) would wipe it once with a cloth of <s>Kāśī</s> (Varanasi silk). By doing so, it would reach complete exhaustion and wearing away; the years, months, days, <s>muhūrtas</s> (moments), <s>nāḍīs</s> (time-units), and <s>kalās</s> (instants) within those periods, down to individual breaths — their measure can be calculated, but the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> cannot be reckoned. Just as, O son of good family, the great ocean is eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> in depth, immeasurable in breadth, extending to the submarine fire — I am able to count each individual drop with a hair-tip split into a hundred parts, but I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Just as, O son of good family, I am able to count each individual leaf of the <s>Śīrṣavana</s> forest, but the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> cannot be reckoned. Just as, O son of good family, if all the men, women, boys, and girls dwelling in the four continents were to become <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the ten stages — the mass of merit of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> would still be less than the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Just as, O son of good family, if in a year of twelve months, or with an intercalary month a year of thirteen months, counting thus by years for a full <s>kalpa</s>, a god were to rain by night and by day — I am able, O son of good family, to count each individual drop, but I am not able, O son of good family, to reckon the mass of merit from a single recitation of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Thus, O son of good family, even if many <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal to me were gathered in one place and supplied for a divine <s>kalpa</s> with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for the sick and all provisions, they would not be sufficient. And even then the <s>Tathāgatas</s> would be unable to reckon the mass of merit of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> — how much less can I alone, dwelling in this world-system! Through inconceivable <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) attainment, O son of good family, I am devoted to the practice of contemplation. And that <s>dharma</s> is subtle, that <s>dharma</s> is unmanifest, that <s>dharma</s> has not yet arrived, it is attained through the deepest heart. It is established through the skillful means of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Thus, O son of good family, seeking to attain the skillful means of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>, I too, O son of good family, have wandered through countless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of world-systems. And having gone before <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with palms joined, tears were shed through the force of the <s>Dharma</s>, for <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> knows the past, future, and present.'

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s>: "I remember, O son of good family, that for the sake of this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī Mahāvidyā</s>, I wandered through world-realms as numerous as atoms of dust. I attended upon many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Yet from those <s>Tathāgatas</s> I did not even hear a semblance of it. Then there was a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Ratnottama</s> (Supreme Jewel), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to Be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. Before him I shed tears. Then that <s>Tathāgata</s>, that <s>Arhat</s>, that Perfectly Awakened One said: 'Do not, O son of good family, shed such pitifully sorrowful tears! Go, son of good family, to the world-realm called <s>Padmottama</s> (Supreme Lotus). There is a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Padmottama</s>. He will grant this <s>Ṣaḍakṣarī</s> (

children.text: tena mamābhihitam - kulaputra ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ rājñīmicchasi bhāvanāyogamanuyuktaḥ? mayoktam - icchāmi sugata / yathā tṛṣārtaḥ pānīyamanveṣate evamahaṃ bhagavan ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ samanveṣamāṇo 'nekalokadhātūnupasaṃkrāntaḥ / paryupāsitāni me 'nekāni tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi, na kasyacitsakāśānmayā labdhā ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā rājñī / tvaṃ bhagavan trātā bhava, śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇam / vikalendriyasya cakṣurbhūto bhava / naṣṭamārgasya darśako bhava / sūryatāpadagdhānāṃ chatrabhūto bhava / caturmahāpathe śālavṛkṣa iva bhava / dharmaparitṛṣisyānantadharmamārgamupadarśako bhava / supratiṣṭhitacetaso vajrakavacabhūto bhava //
children.translated_text: He said to me: 'O son of good family, do you desire the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> (six-syllable great spell), the queen, being devoted to the practice of contemplation?' I said: 'I desire it, O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). Just as one afflicted by thirst seeks water, even so, O Blessed One, seeking the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>, I have approached countless world-systems. I have attended upon countless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, yet from none of them have I obtained the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>, the queen. O Blessed One, be my protector, my refuge, my final resort! Be an eye for one whose faculties are impaired! Be a guide for one who has lost the way! Be a parasol for those scorched by the sun's heat! Be like a <s>śāla</s> tree at the crossroads of four great highways! Be a shower of the inexhaustible <s>Dharma</s> path for those thirsting for the <s>Dharma</s>! Be a vajra-armor for one whose mind is well-established!'

children.text: ) 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ ṣaḍakṣarīmahāvidyāyāḥ kāraṇenānekalokadhātukoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi paribhramitaḥ / dadasva kulaputra ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ rājñīm / tathāgata evaṃ paribhramati //
children.translated_text: 'Look, O son of good family, this <s>Padmottama</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened, has wandered through countless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of world-systems for the sake of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>. Give, O son of good family, the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>, the queen. Thus does the <s>Tathāgata</s> wander.'

children.text: atha avalokiteśvaro bhagavantametadavocat - adṛṣṭamaṇḍalasya na dātavyāṃ kathaṃ bhagavatpadmāṅkamudrāmanugṛhṇāti? kathaṃ maṇidharāṃ mudrāṃ saṃjānīte? kathaṃ sarvarājendrāṃ saṃjānīte? maṇḍalapariśuddhiṃ kathaṃ saṃjānīte? maṇḍalasyedaṃ nimittaṃ caturasraṃ pañcahastapramāṇaṃ sāmantakena madhye maṇḍalasyāmitābhaṃ likhet / indranīlacūrṇaṃ padmarāgacūrṇaṃ marakatacūrṇaṃ sphāṭikacūrṇaṃ suvarṇarūpyacūrṇānyamitābhasya tathāgatasya kāye saṃyojayitavyāni / dakṣiṇe pārśve mahāmaṇidharo bodhisattvaḥ kartavya / vāmapārśve ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā kartavyā caturbhujā śaratkāṇḍagauravarṇā, nānālaṃkāravibhūṣitā / vāmahaste padmaṃ kartavyam / dakṣiṇahaste akṣamālā kartavyā / dau hastau saṃprayuktau sarvarājendrā nāma mudrā kartavyā / tasyāḥ ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyāḥ pādamūle vidyādharaṃ pratisthāpayitavyam / dakṣiṇahaste dhūpakaṭacchukaṃ kartavyaṃ dhūmāyamānam / vāmahaste nānāvidhālaṃkāraparipūrṇaṃ piṭakaṃ kartavyam / tasya ca maṇḍalasya caturdvāreṣu catvāro mahārājāḥ kartavyāḥ, nānāpraharaṇagṛhītāḥ kartavyāḥ / tasya maṇḍalacatuṣkoṇeṣu catvāraḥ pūrṇakumbhāḥ nānāmaṇiratnasaṃcitāḥ / yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā icchati maṇḍalaṃ praveṣṭum, tena sarvagotrasyāparaṃparasya nāmāni likhitavyāni, likhitvā ca haste gṛhītavyāni ca / maṇḍale prathamataraṃ tāni nāmāni prakṣipet / te sarve caramabhavikā bodhisattvā bhavanti / sarvamānuṣyakeṇa duḥkhena viprahīṇā bhaviṣyanti, kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante / tata ācāryeṇa asthāne naiva dātavyā / athavā śraddhādhimuktakasya dātavyā / athavā mahāyānaśraddhādhimuktakasya dātavyā / na ca tīrthikasya dātavyā //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'To one who has not seen the <s>maṇḍala</s>, it should not be given. How does one recognize the <s>Sarvarājendra</s> (lord of all kings) <s>mudrā</s>? How does one recognize the purification of the <s>maṇḍala</s>? The form of the <s>maṇḍala</s> is foursquare, five hand-spans in measure, with a <s>maṇḍala</s> in the center on each side.

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan labheyaṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyā rājñīṃ prāptayogasya? yathā hi bhagavannamṛtasya labdhāsvādāstṛptiṃ na labhante, evamahaṃ bhagavan ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāśrutamātreṇa tṛptiṃ na labhāma / puṇyavantaste sattvā ya imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ japanti śṛṇvanti cintayanti adhyāśayena dhārayanti //

children.text: bhagavānāha - kulaputra, yaścemāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ likhāpayet, tena caturaśītidharmaskandhasahasrāṇi likhāpitāni bhavanti / paramāṇurajopamānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ divyasauvarṇaratnamayān stūpān kārayet, kārayitvā ekadine dhātvāvaropaṇaṃ kuryāt / yaśca teṣāṃ phalavipākaḥ, sa ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyāyā ekasyākṣarasya phalavipākaḥ / acintyo 'guṇānāṃ supratiṣṭhito mokṣaḥ / yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāḥ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ japet, sa imān samādhīn pratilabhate / tadyathā - maṇidharo nāma samādhiḥ, narakatiryaksaṃśodhanaṃ nāma samādhiḥ, vajrakavaco nāma samādhiḥ, supratiṣṭhitacaraṇo nāma samādhiḥ, sarvopāyakauśalyapraveśano nāma samādhiḥ, vikiriṇo nāma samādhiḥ, sarvabuddhakṣetrasaṃdarśano nāma samādhiḥ, sarvadharmapraveśano nāma samādhiḥ, dhyānālaṃkāro nāma samādhiḥ dharmarathābhirūḍho nāma samādhiḥ, rāgadveṣamohaparimokṣaṇo nāma samādhiḥ, anantavatso nāma samādhiḥ, ṣaṭpāramitānirdeśo nāma samādhiḥ, mahāmerudharo nāma samādhiḥ, sarvabhavottāraṇo nāma samādhiḥ, sarvatathāgatavyavalokano nāma samādhiḥ, supratiṣṭhitāsano nāma samādhiḥ / evaṃpramukhānāmaṣṭottarasamādhiśataṃ pratilabhate, ya imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ dhārayati //
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'O son of good family, whoever causes this six-syllable <s>Mahāvidyā</s> to be written, by him the eighty-four thousand collections of <s>Dharma</s> have been caused to be written. It is as if one were to build divine golden jeweled <s>stūpas</s> for <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones numbering as atoms of dust, and having built them, were to install relics in them in a single day. Whatever the fruit and ripening of that merit,

children.text: iti ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyopadeśo nāma pañcamaṃ prakaraṇam //

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - kutrāhaṃ bhagavan gaccheyaṃ yatra ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ labheyam? bhagavānāha - asti kulaputra vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ dharmabhāṇako ya imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyāṃ dhārayati vācayati yoniśaśca manasi kurute / āha - gamiṣyāmyahaṃ bhagavan vārāṇasīṃ mahānagarīṃ tasya dharmabhāṇakasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya / bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, evaṃ kuruṣva / durlabhaste kulaputra dharmabhāṇakastathāgatasamo draṣṭavyaḥ, pūṇyakūṭa iva draṣṭavyaḥ / sarvatīrtho gaṅgeva draṣṭavyaḥ / avitathavādīva draṣṭavyaḥ / bhūtavādīva draṣṭavyaḥ / ratnarāśiriva draṣṭavyaḥ / varadaścintāmaṇiriva draṣṭavyaḥ / dharmarāja iva draṣṭavyaḥ / jagaduttāraṇa iva draṣṭavyaḥ / na ca kulaputra tvayā dharmabhāṇakaṃ dṛṣṭvā vicikitsācittamutpādayitavyam / mā tvaṃ kulaputra bodhisattvabhūmeścyutvā adāye prapatsyase / sa ca dharmabhāṇakaḥ śīlavipannaḥ ācaravipanno bhāryāputraduhitṛbhiḥ parivṛtaḥ kāṣāyoccāraprasrāvaparipūrṇaḥ asaṃvṛtteryāpathaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Where, Blessed One, should I go to obtain the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s> (the great queen of knowledge of six syllables)?' The Blessed One said: 'There is, O son of good family, in the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma) who holds, recites, and wisely contemplates this <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s>.' He said: 'I shall go, Blessed One, to the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for the purpose of seeing, venerating, and attending upon that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Excellent, excellent, O son of good family, do so. That <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> is rare for you; he should be regarded as equal to a <s>Tathāgata</s>, should be regarded as a heap of merit. He should be regarded as the Ganges among all sacred fords. He should be regarded as a speaker of truth. He should be regarded as a speaker of reality. He should be regarded as a heap of jewels. He should be regarded as a wish-granting <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gem bestowing boons. He should be regarded as a king of <s>Dharma</s>. He should be regarded as a savior of the world. And you, O son of good family, having seen the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>, must not generate a mind of doubt. Do not, O son of good family, fall from the stage of a <s>bodhisattva</s> and descend into an unfavorable state. That <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> is one whose moral conduct is impaired, whose behavior is impaired, who is surrounded by wife, sons, and daughters, who is filled with the filth of excrement and urine, and whose deportment is unrestrained.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - yathājñaptaṃ bhagavatā / atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bodhisattvo mahāsattva anekairbodhisattvaparṣadgṛhasthaiḥ pravrajitairdārakadārikādibhiḥ saṃprasthitaḥ / tasya dharmabhāṇakasya pūjākarmaṇe divyāni chatrāṇi divyāni upānahāni maulīkuṇḍalasragdāmakeyūrahārārdhahāraratnahāraskandhopariṣvajānikapṛṣṭhottaryāṇi aṅguṣṭhavibhedikāni anyāni ca vividhāni vastrāṇi cīvarādhyuṣitāni vidyādharasaṃcoditāni kāśikavastrāṇyagniśaucavastrāṇi ca anyāni ca vividhāni vastrāṇi puṣpāṇi / tadyathā - utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamāndāravamahāmāndāravāṇi mañjūṣakamahāmañjūṣakāṇi caudumbarāṇi anyāni vividhāni kāṣṭhapuṣpāṇi campakakaravīrapāṭalāni muktakavārṣikāṇi śakunakādhyuṣitāni / sumanānavamālikacakravākopaśobhitāni / śālikautsukyāni śatapatrikāṇi nīlapītalohitāvadātamāñjiṣṭhasphaṭikarajatavarṇāni / anyāni ca sthalajalajāni puṣpāṇi vividhāni gṛhītvā yena vārāṇasī mahānagarī tenopajagāma / anupūrveṇa vārāṇasīṃ mahānagarīmanuprāptaḥ / yena sa dharmabhāṇakastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya pādau śirasābhivandya sa tena dṛṣṭaḥ śīlavipanna ācāravipanno 'saṃvṛteryāpathaḥ / tena tāṇi chātrāṇyupānahāni vastrābharaṇāni gandhamālyavilepanānyupaḍhaukitāni / tairvastrābharaṇaiḥ gandhamālyaiśca mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tasya dharmabhāṇakasya purastātprāñjalībhūtaḥ tadvijñamidamavocat - aho dharmanidhānāsvādako 'mṛtanidhiriva saṃcaya anavagāho 'si, sāgaro yathā bhājanabhūto 'si sarvamānuṣyabhūteṣu eva te / tava sakāśāddharmaṃ deśayataḥ devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garūḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ sarve te saṃnipatitāḥ / tava dharmaśravaṇakāle mahāvajrasamaye dharmaparyāyaṃ nirdiśasi parimokṣayasi / bahavaḥ sattvā ye saṃsāre bandhanabaddhāḥ / puṇyavantaste sattvāḥ ye 'syāṃ vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ vasanti, paśyanti, tava satataṃ parigrahaṃ kurvanti / darśanamātreṇa sarvapāpāni nirdahasi / yathāgnirdahati vanāntaram, (
Vaidya 299

children.text: ) evaṃ tvaṃ darśanena sarvapāpāni dahasi / jānante tava tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ / anye cānekabodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi tava pūjākarmaṇa upasaṃkrāmanti / brahmāviṣṇumaheśvaracandrādityavāyuvaruṇāgnayo yamaśca dharmarājo 'nye ca catvāro mahārājānaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) so too do you burn away all sins by your very sight. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones know you. And other countless hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> approach to make offerings to you — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), <s>Varuṇa</s> (Water), <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Yama</s> the king of <s>Dharma</s>, and the other four great kings.'

Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'As the Blessed One has instructed.' Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, accompanied by many <s>bodhisattvas</s>, assemblies of householders, renunciants, boys, girls, and others, set out for the purpose of making offerings to that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> — with divine parasols, divine sandals, diadems, earrings, garlands, wreaths, armlets, necklaces, half-necklaces, jeweled necklaces, shoulder shawls, back garments, finger-rings, and various other garments and robes inhabited by <s>vidyādharas</s> (knowledge-holders), fabrics of <s>Kāśī</s>, fire-purified cloths, and various other garments and flowers. Namely: <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white water lily), <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus), <s>māndārava</s> and <s>mahāmāndārava</s> flowers, <s>mañjūṣaka</s> and <s>mahāmañjūṣaka</s> flowers, <s>audumbara</s> (fig blossoms), and various other tree-flowers — <s>campaka</s>, <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), <s>pāṭala</s>, <s>muktaka</s>, <s>vārṣika</s>, and flowers frequented by birds; adorned with <s>sumanā</s> (jasmine), <s>navamālikā</s> (jasmine), and <s>cakravāka</s> flowers; <s>śāli</s> blossoms and hundred-petaled flowers in blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, crystal, and silver hues; and various other flowers of land and water. Taking these, he went to the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Gradually he reached the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. He approached that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>. Having approached, he bowed at his feet with his head. He saw him — impaired in moral conduct, impaired in behavior, with unrestrained deportment. He presented those parasols, sandals, garments, ornaments, perfumes, garlands, and ointments. Having made a great offering with those garments, ornaments, perfumes, and garlands, standing before that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> with palms joined, he spoke this wise word: 'O you who relish the treasure of <s>Dharma</s>, you are like a storehouse of the immortal nectar, unfathomable like the ocean. You are a vessel among all human beings. When you teach the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans — all of them assemble. At the time of hearing your <s>Dharma</s>, at the great <s>vajra</s> occasion, you expound and liberate through the <s>Dharma</s> discourse. Many are the beings who are bound in the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Fortunate are those beings who dwell in this great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, who see you and constantly attend upon you. By the mere sight of you, all sins are burned away. Just as fire burns the interior of a forest (

children.text: athe sa dharmabhāṇakastasyaitadavocat - mā tvaṃ kulaputra kaukṛtyamutpādayasi / kati māṣāḥ kleṣā aupabhogikāḥ saṃsārasya naimittikāḥ prajāmaṇḍalasyotpādikāḥ / ye ca kulaputrāḥ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ jānante, na ca te rāgeṇa dveṣeṇa mohena saṃlipyante / yathā jāmbūnadasya suvarṇasya na sajjate malam, evameva kulaputra yasya ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā kāyagatā, na tasya kāyena na rāgeṇa na dveṣeṇa na mohena saṃlipyate //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> said this to him: 'Do not, O son of good family, generate remorse. How many are the defilements that are objects of enjoyment, causes of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and producers of the circle of beings! Those sons of good family who know the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s> are not stained by passion, hatred, or delusion. Just as no impurity clings to gold from the <s>Jāmbūnada</s> river, even so, O son of good family, for one in whose body the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā</s> dwells, neither his body nor passion, nor hatred, nor delusion can stain him.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī gāḍhaṃ pāde pariṣvajyainametadavocat - vikalendriyasya cakṣurbhūto bhava / naṣṭamārgasyopadarśako bhava / dharmaparitṛṣitasya dharmarasena saṃtarpaya me tvam / anuttarāsamyaksaṃbodhiviprahīṇasya bodhibījaṃ me dadasva / dharmāṇāmavakāśaṃ dadasva / supratiṣṭhitarūpāṇāṃ kāyapariśuddhiṃ dadasva / abhedyānāṃ kuśalānāṃ pratilambha iti sarvajanāḥ kathayanti vākyaṃ madhuropacayam / evaṃ gururdadasva me ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ yenāhaṃ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho bhaveyam / dvādaśākāraṃ dharmarandhra(cakra?)māvartayeyam / sarvasattvānāṃ sāṃsārikaṃ duḥkhaṃ parimocayeyam / ṣaḍakṣarīmahāvidyārājñīlabdhalābho bhaveyam / dadasva me ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyārājñīm / trātā bhava, śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇam / advīpānāṃ dvipo bhava //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, firmly embracing his feet, said this to him: 'Be an eye to one whose faculties are impaired! Be a guide to one who has lost the path! Satisfy me, who thirsts for the <s>Dharma</s>, with the essence of the <s>Dharma</s>! Give me the seed of awakening, who has been separated from <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)! Grant an opening to the <s>Dharma</s>! Grant purity of body to those of well-established form! All people say these words of sweet accumulation: "Grant attainment of indestructible wholesome qualities." Thus, O teacher, give me the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s>, by which I may quickly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, turn the <s>Dharma</s> wheel of twelve aspects, liberate all beings from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and obtain the benefit of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s>! Give me the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s>! Be a protector, a refuge, a recourse! Be an island for those without an island!'

children.text: atha sa dharmabhāṇakastasyaitadavocat - durlabhaṃ ṣaḍakṣarimahāvidyārājñyā asamavajrapadam / abhedyavajrapadam / anuttarajñānadarśanapadam / akṣayajñānapadam / niruttarapadam / mokṣapraveśanapadam / tathāgatajñānaviśuddhipadam / rāgadveṣamohasaṃsāraduḥkhaparivarjanapadam / sarvopāyakauśalyapadam / dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpūrtipadam / sarvadharmapraviśanapadam / nityakāladevatābhikāṅkṣipadam / ye ca kulaputrā nānāsthāneṣu dīkṣante / mokṣārtheṣu nānāpaṭeṣu dīkṣante / tadyathā indrapaṭaṃ śvetapaṭaṃ dhyuṣitapaṭam / divasanirīkṣakā maheśvareṣu dīkṣante / bailmavegarūdreṣu nagnaśramaṇeṣu ca / eṣu sthāneṣu dīkṣante / na teṣāṃ mokṣaṃ saṃvidyate / anādigatikānāmapi nāpi nāśo bhavati / sarvadevagaṇāśca brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ śakraśca devānāmindraścandrādityau vāyuvaruṇādayo yamaśca dharmarājo catvāraśca mahārājānaḥ, te nityakālaṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahavidyārājñīṃ prārthayanti //
children.translated_text: Then that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> said this to him: 'Rare is the syllable of the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s> — the unequaled <s>vajra</s> syllable, the indestructible <s>vajra</s> syllable, the syllable of supreme knowledge and insight, the syllable of inexhaustible knowledge, the unsurpassed syllable, the syllable that is the gateway to liberation, the syllable of the purity of <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge, the syllable that eliminates the suffering of passion, hatred, delusion, and <s>saṃsāra</s>, the syllable of all skillful means, the syllable of the fulfillment of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the syllable that enters all <s>dharmas</s>, the syllable desired by the gods at all times. Those sons of good family who are initiated in various places, who are initiated for the purpose of liberation in various cloths — such as the <s>Indra</s>-cloth, the white cloth, the consecrated cloth — those who observe the sun and are initiated among the followers of <s>Maheśvara</s>, among the <s>Rudras</s> with the speed of <s>Bel</s>, and among the naked ascetics — those who are initiated in these traditions, for them there is no liberation. For those of beginningless destiny, there is no destruction either. All the hosts of gods — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Śakra</s> the lord of the <s>devas</s>, <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), <s>Varuṇa</s> (Water) and others, <s>Yama</s> the king of <s>Dharma</s>, and the four great kings — they all constantly seek the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s>.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī tamāha - kathaṃ vayaṃ ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ labhemahi yena vayaṃ kṣipravarā bhavāmaḥ? dharmabhāṇakastamuvāca - tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin prajñāpāramitānirjātāḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ / tatprajñāpāramitā sarvatathāgatānāṃ ca netrītyākhyāyate / sāpi ca ṣaḍakṣarīṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ praṇamate kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhavantī, prāgeva tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvagaṇāḥ / ida kulaputra taṇḍulavatsāraṃ mahāyānasya kiṃcidasau bahumahāyānasūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇagāthānidānetivṛttajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmopadeśakaḥ prāpyante(?) Vaidya 300

children.text: ) kulaputra japitamātreṇa śivaṃ mokṣam, kiṃbahunā anyakuśalamiti / kiṃvā tu samadhyagataṃ sāramupagṛhṇanti śālinastathā sāramityanugṛhṇanti, nītvā svakīye niveśane bhāṇḍāni paripūrṇāni kṛtvā sthāpayitvā divasānurūpeṇa sūryatāpena pariśoṣayitvā musalaprahārairvibhedayanti, tataścaturvarṣāṇi parityajanti / kiṃ sāramiti vyavasthitam? taṇḍulasāramiti / evamevānye yogāḥ tuṣasadṛśāḥ / sarvayogānāṃ ceyaṃ ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā rājñī taṇḍulamiti bhūtā draṣṭavyā / yasyāḥ kāraṇena kulaputra bodhisattvāḥ śrāvayanto bhramanti dānapāramitārthinaḥ, śīlapāramitārthinaḥ, kṣāntipāramitārthinaḥ vīryapāramitārthinaḥ, dhyānapāramitārthinaḥ, prajñāpāramitārthinaḥ / ekajāpena kulaputra ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayanti / yasya kasyacidvastrasparśanenāpi avaivartikabhūmiṃ pratilabhante / evamevāsyāḥ ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyā rājñī, durlabhamasyā nāmagrahaṇam / ekavāranāmagrahaṇena sarve tathāgatāścīvarapiṇḍapātraśayyāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkaraiḥ sarvopasthānairupasthitā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: O son of good family, by mere recitation one attains auspiciousness and liberation — what need is there to speak of other merits? Or consider: people take the essence that has ripened, they gather the essence of rice — having taken it to their own dwelling, having filled and stored their vessels, having dried it in the sun's heat over the days, they separate it by striking with a pestle, and then discard the four husks. What is established as the essence? The essence of rice-grain. Even so, other spiritual practices are like the husk. And this six-syllable great <s>vidyā</s> queen is the rice-grain essence of all spiritual practices — thus it should be seen. For the sake of which, O son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> wander proclaiming it, seeking the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), seeking the perfection of discipline (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), seeking the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), seeking the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), seeking the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), seeking the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). By a single recitation, O son of good family, the six perfections are fulfilled. By the mere touch of one's garment, one attains the stage of non-retrogression (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>). Such is this six-syllable great <s>vidyā</s> queen; rare is even the grasping of her name. By a single utterance of her name, all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are served with all requisites — robes, alms-bowls, beds, seats, and medicines for the sick.

Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said to him: 'How may we obtain the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s> by which we may quickly become foremost?' The <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> said to him: 'Just as, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, all <s>Tathāgatas</s> are born from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), and that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is called the guide of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, even she bows down to the <s>ṣaḍakṣarī mahāvidyārājñī</s> with palms joined — how much more so the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, and the hosts of <s>bodhisattvas</s>! This, O son of good family, is the essence of rice, as it were, of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; this great <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>, with its verses, explanations, songs, narratives, previous births, extensive teachings, marvels, and doctrinal instructions, is obtained (

Supremely resplendent gardens, supremely adorned, wonderful, and most delightful; divine lotus ponds and hundreds of thousands of delightful peaked pavilions made of divine gold and jewels, with festoons of pearls hanging down, with hundreds of thousands of pearl necklaces hanging down. Beneath those peaked pavilions is a wish-fulfilling jewel called <s>Sārada</s>, which provides all requisites for those <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Having gone, they sit cross-legged, holding the body upright, establishing mindfulness before them. Such, O son of good family, are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who dwell in that hair-pore. Then, O son of good family, descending from that hair-pore, there is a hair-pore called <s>Indrarāja</s> (King Indra).
