children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Has <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> not yet come, O Blessed One?' The Blessed One replied: '<s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is coming, O son of good family. He is coming to this very <s>Jetavana</s> great monastery for the purpose of seeing me, paying homage, and attending upon me, and also for the purpose of giving a prophecy of awakening (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) to the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Maheśvara</s> in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm.'

children.text: athāvalokiteśvareṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena raśmaya utsṛṣṭā nīlapītalohitāvadātamāñjiṣṭhasphaṭikarajatavarṇāḥ / te ca raśmayo jetavanamāgacchanti / āgatya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya punareva jetavanādvihārānniṣkramya avīciṃ mahānarakaṃ gacchanti / tatra gatvā avīcimahānarakaṃ śītibhāvamupanayanti / atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - kuto bhagavan raśmaya āgacchanti kutra gacchanti? bhagavānāha - evaṃ kulaputra avalokiteśvareṇa nānāvidhā raśmaya utsṛṣṭāḥ / te cāsmin jetavane vihāramāgacchanti / āgatya ca māṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya avīciṃ mahānarakaṃ gacchanti / gatvā cāvīcimahānarakaṃ śītibhāvaṃ kurvanti / tasmin jetavane vihāre śubhanimittāni prādurbhūtāni / divyāni campakavṛkṣāṇi prādurbhūtāni / divyāḥ puṣkariṇyaḥ prādurbhūtāḥ / tatra jetavanavihāre divyasauvarṇanirbhāsā dṛśyante / īdṛśo jetavanavihāro dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, emitted rays of blue, yellow, red, white, <s>māñjiṣṭha</s> (crimson), crystal, and silver colors. Those rays came to <s>Jetavana</s>. Having arrived, they circumambulated the Blessed One three times and then, departing again from the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery, went to the great hell of <s>Avīci</s>. Having gone there, they brought coolness to the great hell of <s>Avīci</s>,

children.text: athāvalokiteśvaraḥ sukhāvatīlokadhātorniṣkramya yena jetavanavihārastena saṃprasthitaḥ / anupūrveṇa jetavanavihāraṃ saṃprāptaḥ / atha tasmin jetavanavihāre praviṣṭo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte sthitaḥ / tadā kalaviṅkarutasvarābhinirghoṣeṇa bhagavānārocayati - āgatastvaṃ kulaputra? kṛtaste sattvaparīpākaḥ? athāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - yathājñapto bhagavatā / evaṃ ca mayā karmabhūmirniṣpāditā / atha bhagavān sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputra, yastvayā īdṛśā karmabhūmirniṣpāditā / athāvalokiteśvaro bhagavantaṃ padmānyupanāmayati - imāni te bhagavannamitābhena tathāgatena prahitāni / pṛcchatyalpābādhatāṃ ca alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca sukhasparśavihāratāṃ ca / tato bhagavatā gṛhītvā vāmapārśve sthāpitāni //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, departing from the <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Pure Land) world-realm, set forth toward the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery. Gradually he arrived at the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery. Having entered the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Then the Blessed One addressed him with a voice like the song of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird: 'Have you arrived, O son of good family? Have you accomplished your task?'

children.text: atha maheśvaro devaputro yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantametadavocat - labheyāhaṃ bhagavan vyākaraṇanirdeśasya samuddeśam? bhagavānāha - (
Vaidya 304
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 304]

children.text: ) gaccha kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaste vyākaraṇaṃ dāsyati / atha maheśvaro devaputro 'valokiteśvarasya pādayornipatya stotraviśeṣaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ -
children.translated_text: 'Go, O son of good family — <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, will give you the prophecy.' Then the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>, having prostrated at the feet of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, began to offer a special hymn of praise:

Then the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Maheśvara</s> approached the Blessed One, and having approached, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and said this to the Blessed One: 'May I obtain, O Blessed One, the proclamation of my prophecy of awakening (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>)?' The Blessed One said:

children.text: namostvalokiteśvarāya maheśvarāya padmadharāya padmāsanāya padmapriyāya śubhapadmahastāya padmaśriye parivṛtāya jagadāsvādanakarāya pṛthivīvaralocanakarāya prahlādanakarāya //
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, to the Great Lord, to the Lotus-Bearer, to the Lotus-Seated, to the Lotus-Lover, to the One with the Auspicious Lotus in Hand, to the One Surrounded by Lotus-Glory, to the One Who Brings Delight to the World, to the One Whose Eyes Survey the Excellent Earth, to the One Who Brings Joy!

children.text: evaṃ maheśvaro devaputro gatvā avalokiteśvarasya stotraviśeṣaṃ kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ / atha avalokiteśvarastametadavocat - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tvaṃ kulaputra tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ? atha maheśvaro devaputrastametadavocat - dadasva me vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / avalokiteśvarastametadavocat - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputra vivṛtāyāṃ lokadhātau bhasmeśvaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / atha sā umādevyupasaṃkramyāvalokiteśvarasya pādau śirasā vanditvā avalokiteśvarasya stotrābhidhānaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s>, having gone and offered this special hymn of praise to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, remained in silence. Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> spoke this to him: "Why, O son of good family, do you remain in silence?" Then the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s> spoke this to him: "Grant me a prophecy of unsurpassed perfect awakening." <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> spoke this to him: "You, O son of good family, shall become in the world-realm called Vivṛtā a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Bhasmeśvara</s> (Lord of Ashes), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to Be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>." Then the goddess <s>Umā</s>, having approached and bowed her head at the feet of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, began to utter a hymn of praise to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>:

children.text: namo 'stvalokiteśvarāya meheśvarāya prāṇaṃdadāya pṛthivīvaralocanakarāya śubhapadmaśriye parivṛtāya nirvāṇabhūmisaṃprasthitāya sucetanakarāya dharmadharāya //
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, to the Great Lord, to the Giver of Breath, to the One Whose Eyes Survey the Excellent Earth, to the One Surrounded by Auspicious Lotus-Glory, to the One Proceeding to the Ground of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, to the One Who Brings Good Awareness, to the Bearer of <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: evaṃ sā umādevī stotrābhidhānaṃ kṛtvā avalokiteśvarasya pratyāhāraṃ kartumārabdhā -
children.translated_text: Thus the goddess <s>Umā</s>, having uttered the hymn of praise, began to make a request of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>:

children.text: parimocaya me strībhāvājjugupsanīyāt / kalimalaparipūrṇagarbhāvāsaduḥkhāt satataparigrahasaṃgṛhītāt parimokṣaya mām / athāvalokiteśvarastāmetadavocat - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ bhagini umeśvaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / himavataḥ parvatarājasya dakṣiṇe pārśve tava lokadhāturbhaviṣyati / atha sā umādevī vyākaraṇamanuprāptā //
children.translated_text: "Liberate me from the despised state of womanhood! Free me from the suffering of dwelling in the womb, filled with the impurity of the age of <s>Kali</s>, constantly seized by attachment!" Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> spoke this to her: "You, O sister, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Umeśvara</s> (Lord of Umā), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to Be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. On the southern slope of <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, your world-realm shall be." Then the goddess <s>Umā</s> received the prophecy.

children.text: bhagavānāha - paśya sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin / vyākṛtā umādevī avalokiteśveraṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarve te 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Behold, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>! The goddess <s>Umā</s> was given a prophecy by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — all of them for unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: ayaṃ kulaputra maheśvaranirvyūho nāma khyāta iti //
children.translated_text: "This, O son of good family, is known as the 'Array of <s>Maheśvara</s>.'"

children.text: START Kvyu 2,8:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Kāraṇḍavyūha, section 2.8]

children.text: aṣṭamaṃ prakaraṇam /
children.translated_text: The eighth chapter.

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - āgato bhagavannavalokiteśvaraḥ / yathāndhabhūtena cakṣuranuprāptam, evaṃ bhagavannavalokiteśvaro 'nuprāptaḥ / adya me saphalaṃ janma / adya me āśā paripūrṇā / adya me pariśodhito bodhimārgaḥ / sa cetanasadharmakāyanirvāṇopadarśakam //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Avalokiteśvara</s> has arrived, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Just as sight is regained by one who was blind, so has <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> arrived, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. Today my birth is fruitful. Today my hope is fulfilled. Today the path of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) is purified for me. He is the one who shows the sentient <s>Dharmakāya</s> and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>."

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī punareva bhagavantametadavocat - adyāsmākaṃ bhagavan deśaya tvamavalokiteśvarasya guṇaviśeṣam //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī</s> spoke again to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Today, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, teach us the special qualities of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>."

children.text: bhagavānāha - tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin cakravālamahācakravālau parvatarājānau / mucilindamahāmucilindau parvatarājānau / kālamahākālau parvatarājānau / saṃsṛṣṭamahāsaṃsṛṣṭau parvatarājānau / pralambodaraḥ parvatarājā / anādarśakaḥ parvatarājā / (
Vaidya 305
children.translated_text: [Vaidya edition, page 305]

children.text: ) kṛtsrāgataḥ parvatarājā / jālinīmukhaḥ parvatarājā / śataśṛṅgaḥ parvatarājā / bhavanaśca parvatarājā / mahāmaṇiratnaḥ parvatarājā / sudarśanaśca parvatarājā / akāladarśanaśca parvatarājā / eteṣu parvatarājeṣvekaikaṃ lokadhātuṣu śakyate mayā parvatarājānāṃ palāni vā palaśatāni vā palasahasrāṇi vā palakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi vā saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi śakyate mayā kulaputra gaṇayitum / na tu kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya śakyate puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra śakyate mayā paramāṇurajasāṃ pramāṇamudgṛhītum, na tu kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya śakyate puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra śakyate mayā mahāsamudrasyaikaikaṃ binduṃ gaṇayitum, na tu kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya śakyate mayā puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra śakyate mayā śīrṣavanasyaikaikāni patrāṇi gaṇayitum, na tu kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya śakyate puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ gaṇayitum //
children.translated_text: ) <s>Kṛtsrāgata</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Jālinīmukha</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Śataśṛṅga</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Bhavana</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Mahāmaṇiratna</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Sudarśana</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Akāladarśana</s>, the king of mountains — among these kings of mountains, for each one in each world-realm, I could count the weight in <s>palas</s> (measures), or hundreds of <s>palas</s>, or thousands of <s>palas</s>, or hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>palas</s> — I could count the measure, the fraction, the number, O son of good family. But, O son of good family, the accumulation of merit of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> cannot be counted. Just as, O son of good family, I could grasp the measure of atoms of dust, but the accumulation of merit of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> cannot be counted. Just as, O son of good family, I could count each drop of the great ocean, but the accumulation of merit of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> cannot be counted by me. Just as, O son of good family, I could count each leaf of the Śīrṣa forest, but the accumulation of merit of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> cannot be counted."

The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Just as, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, there are <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s>, the kings of mountains; <s>Mucilinda</s> and <s>Mahāmucilinda</s>, the kings of mountains; <s>Kāla</s> and <s>Mahākāla</s>, the kings of mountains; <s>Saṃsṛṣṭa</s> and <s>Mahāsaṃsṛṣṭa</s>, the kings of mountains; <s>Pralambodara</s>, the king of mountains; <s>Anādarśaka</s>, the king of mountains; (

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra sumeruḥ parvatarājo bhūryarāśirbhavet / mahāsamudraḥ bheraṇḍumaṇḍalaṃ bhavet / caturdvīpanivāsinaḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikādayaḥ sarve te lekhakā bhaveyuḥ / sa ca sumeruparvatarājo 'nanto likhito bhavet / śakyate mayaikaikākṣaraṃ gaṇayitum / na tvavalokiteśvarasya śakyate puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ gaṇayitum / tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin dvādaśa gaṅgānadīvālukopamāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāścīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ samupasthitā bhaveyuḥ / yaśca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmupasthāne puṇyaskandhaḥ, tataḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvarasyaikavālāgre puṇyaskandhaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin avalokiteśvaraḥ anekaiḥ samādhiśataiḥ samanvāgataḥ / tadyathā - prabhaṃjano nāma samādhiḥ / vibhūṣaṇakalo nāma samādhiḥ / abhūṣaṇakaro nāma samādhiḥ / vidyullocano nāma samādhiḥ / kṣapaṇo nāma samādhiḥ / mahāmanasvī nāma samadhiḥ / ākārakaro nāma samādhiḥ / vajramālā nāma samādhiḥ / varado nāma samādhiḥ / śatavīryo nāma samādhiḥ / andhavyūho nāma samādhiḥ / pratibhānakūṭo nāma samādhiḥ / rājendro nāma samādhiḥ / vajraprākāro nāma samādhiḥ / vajramukho nāma samādhiḥ / sadāvaradāyako nāma samādhiḥ / indriyaparimocano nāma samādhiḥ / dveṣaparimocano nāma samādhiḥ / candravaralocano nāma samādhiḥ / divākaravaralocano nāma samādhiḥ / dharmābhimukho nāma samādhiḥ / vajrakukṣirnāma samādhiḥ / sudarśako nāma samādhiḥ / nirvāṇakaro nāma samādhiḥ / anantaraśminiṣpādanakaro nāma samādhiḥ / yogakaro nāma samādhiḥ / vikiriṇo nāma samādhiḥ / jambudvīpavaralocano nāma samādhiḥ / buddhakṣetravaralocano nāma samādhiḥ / maitryābhimukho nāma samādhiḥ / prajñāpratibhāsito nāma samādhiḥ / sudanto nāma samādhiḥ / akṣarākṣaro nāma samādhiḥ / avīcisaṃśoṣaṇo nāma samādhiḥ / sāgaragambhīro nāma samādhiḥ / śataparivāro nāma samādhiḥ / mārgasaṃdarśano nāma samādhiḥ / ebhiḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvaraḥ samanvāgataḥ //
children.translated_text: "Just as, O son of good family, Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, were to become a heap of earth, and the great ocean were to become a circle of ink, and all the inhabitants of the four continents — men, women, boys, and girls — were all to become scribes, and that Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, were to be written upon endlessly — I could count each syllable, but the accumulation of merit of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> cannot be counted. Just as, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, if <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones equal in number to the grains of sand of twelve Ganges rivers were attended upon with robes, alms-food, bowls, bedding, seats, medicine for the sick, and all requisites — the mass of merit from attending upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s> would equal the mass of merit on a single hair-tip of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, O son of good family. Just as, O <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is endowed with many hundreds of <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions), namely: the <s>samādhi</s> called Storm-Wind, the <s>samādhi</s> called Ornament-Time, the <s>samādhi</s> called Adorning-Maker, the <s>samādhi</s> called Lightning-Eye, the <s>samādhi</s> called Destroyer, the <s>samādhi</s> called Great-Minded, the <s>samādhi</s> called Form-Maker, the <s>samādhi</s> called Vajra-Garland, the <s>samādhi</s> called Boon-Granter, the <s>samādhi</s> called Hundred-Powers, the <s>samādhi</s> called Blind-Array, the <s>samādhi</s> called Peak of Eloquence, the <s>samādhi</s> called Lord of Kings, the <s>samādhi</s> called Vajra-Rampart, the <s>samādhi</s> called Vajra-Face, the <s>samādhi</s> called Ever-Granting-Boons, the <s>samādhi</s> called Liberating the Senses, the <s>samādhi</s> called Liberating Hatred, the <s>samādhi</s> called Excellent Moon-Eye, the <s>samādhi</s> called Excellent Sun-Eye, the <s>samādhi</s> called Facing the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>samādhi</s> called Vajra-Womb, the <s>samādhi</s> called Beautiful-to-Behold, the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-Maker, the <s>samādhi</s> called Producer of Infinite Rays, the <s>samādhi</s> called Yoga-Maker, the <s>samādhi</s> called Scatterer, the <s>samādhi</s> called Excellent Survey of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the <s>samādhi</s> called Excellent Survey of Buddha-Fields, the <s>samādhi</s> called Facing Loving-Kindness, the <s>samādhi</s> called Illuminated by Wisdom, the <s>samādhi</s> called Well-Tamed, the <s>samādhi</s> called Syllable and Non-Syllable, the <s>samādhi</s> called Drying Up Avīci, the <s>samādhi</s> called Ocean-Deep, the <s>samādhi</s> called Hundred Retinues, the <s>samādhi</s> called Path-Shower. With these, O son of good family, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is endowed."

children.text: Vaidya 306

tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra krakucchando nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / tena kālena tena samayena ahaṃ dānaśūro nāma bodhisattvo 'bhūvam / tadā etasya tathāgatasya puraḥ sthitvā īdṛśamavalokiteśvarasamantabhadrayoḥ samādhivigraho mayā dṛṣṭaḥ / bhadrādibhiścānyairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ samādhivigraho dṛṣṭaḥ / yadā samantabhadro bodhisattvo vajrodgataṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vividhamādhisamādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadraścandravaralocanaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadāvalokiteśvaraḥ sūryavaralocanaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadro vicchuritaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadāvalokiteśvaro gaganagañjaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadra ākārakaraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadāvalokiteśvara indramatiṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadro bhadrarājaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadā avalokiteśvaraḥ sāgaragambhīraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadraḥ siṃhaviṣkambhitaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadāvalokiteśvaraḥ siṃhavikrīḍitaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadro varadāyakaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede, tadāvalokiteśvaraḥ avīcisaṃśoṣaṇaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / yadā samantabhadraḥ sarvaromavivarāṇyuddhāṭayati, tadāvalokiteśvaraḥ sarvaromavivarāṇyapāvṛṇoti / tadā samantabhadrastametadavocat - sādhu sādhvavalokiteśvara, yastvamīdṛśaṃ pratibhānavān / atha krakucchandastathāgatastametadavocat - alpaṃ tvayā kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya pratibhānaṃ dṛṣṭam / yādṛśamavalokiteśvarasya pratibhānaṃ tādṛśaṃ tathāgatānāṃ na saṃvidyate / īdṛśaṃ mayā kulaputra krakucchandasya tathāgatasya sakāśācchrutam //
children.translated_text: Just so, <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, in a former time, O son of good family, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world — a Worthy One, Perfectly Enlightened, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone), Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Blessed One. At that time, at that occasion, I was a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dānaśūra</s> (Hero of Generosity). Then, standing before that <s>Tathāgata</s>, I witnessed such a contest of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) between <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> and <s>Samantabhadra</s>. <s>Bhadra</s> and other <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> also witnessed the <s>samādhi</s> contest. When <s>Samantabhadra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vajrodgata</s> (Vajra-Arisen), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vividhamādhi</s> (Manifold Attainment). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Candravaralocana</s> (Excellent Moon-Eye), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sūryavaralocana</s> (Excellent Sun-Eye). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vicchurita</s> (Radiant), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Gaganagañja</s> (Sky Treasury). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ākārakara</s> (Form-Maker), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Indramati</s> (Indra's Wisdom). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Bhadrarāja</s> (King of Auspiciousness), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sāgaragambhīra</s> (Ocean-Deep). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Siṃhaviṣkambhita</s> (Lion's Suppression), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s> (Lion's Sport). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Varadāyaka</s> (Boon-Granter), then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Avīcisaṃśoṣaṇa</s> (Drying Up of <s>Avīci</s> Hell). When <s>Samantabhadra</s> opened all pores of his body, then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> uncovered all pores of his body. Then <s>Samantabhadra</s> said to him: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, that you are so brilliantly eloquent!' Then <s>Krakucchanda</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> said to him: 'You have seen only a small portion of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>'s eloquence, O son of good family. Such eloquence as <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>'s is not found even among the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.' Thus did I hear from the presence of <s>Krakucchanda</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, O son of good family.

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavān kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ yena vayaṃ dharmarasenāpūryamāṇāḥ saṃtṛptāḥ bhavema / bhagavānāha - ye kulaputra kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānasūtraratnarājasya nāma śroṣyanti, teṣāṃ pūrvakāni karmāvaraṇāni na saṃvidyante / ye paradāragamanaprasaktā aurabhrikakarmodyuktāḥ, ye mātāpitṛghātakā arhaddhātastūpabhedakāstathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarudhirotpādakāḥ, īdṛśānāṃ pāparatānāṃ sattvānāṃ tadapi kāraṇḍavyūho mahāyānasūtraratnarājaḥ sarvapāpaparimokṣaṇaṃ kurute //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, so that we, being filled with the flavor of the <s>Dharma</s>, may be satisfied.' The Blessed One said: 'Those sons of good family who will hear the name of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s> — for them, former <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations) will not exist. Those who are devoted to adultery, those engaged in the killing of sheep, those who have killed their mother or father, those who have split the <s>stūpa</s> of a Worthy One's relics, those who have produced evil-minded blood in the presence of a <s>Tathāgata</s> — even for such beings delighting in sin, the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, brings about complete liberation from all sins.'

children.text: atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhī bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ jānāmyahaṃ bhagavan kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ sarvapāpaparimokṣaṇaṃ kurute? bhagavānāha - asti kulaputra sumeroḥ parvatarājasya dakṣiṇapārśve saptabhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairmalanirmalau tīrthau parikalpitau / etarhi mayā vikalpitau / yathā pāṇḍulavastraṃ nīlamanugacchanti, sa pāparāśiriva draṣṭavyaḥ / evameva kulaputra idaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ sarvapāpāni dahati / suśuklabhāvaṃ kurute / tadyathāpi nāma sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin varṣākālasamaye sarvāṇi tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ sarve nīlābhi(rūpā) bhavanti / atha śatamukho nāma nāgarājaḥ bhavanādavatīrya sarvāstā tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatīrdahati / evamevāyaṃ kulaputraṃ kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ sarvapāpāni dahati, śuklabhāvaṃ kurute / sukhitāste sattvā bhaviṣyanti, ya imaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraṃ ratnarājaṃ (
Vaidya 307
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 307]

children.text: ) śroṣyanti / na te kulaputra pṛthagjanā iti vaktavyāḥ / avaivartikā bodhisattvā iva draṣṭavyāḥ / teṣāṃ ca maraṇakāraṇasamaye dvādaśa tathāgatā upasaṃkramya āśvāsayanti - mā bhaiṣīḥ kulaputra / tvayā kāraṇḍavyūhaṃ mahāyānasūtraratnarājaṃ śrutam / na tvayā punareva saṃsāraṃ saṃsaritavyam / na punarapi teṣāṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / tata iṣṭapriyaviprayogo priyasaṃprayogo na bhaviṣyati / gamiṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputra sukhāvatilokadhātum / amitābhasya tathāgatasya sakāśāddharmamanuśroṣyasi / evaṃ kulaputra teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sukhamaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / athāvalokiteśvaro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte prakrāntaḥ / atha sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhistūṣṇīṃbhāvena vyavasthitaḥ / ta ca devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garūḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ prakrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: hear this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>. They should not be called ordinary beings, O son of good family. They should be regarded as non-retrogressing <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And at the time of their death, twelve <s>Tathāgatas</s> will approach and console them: 'Do not be afraid, O son of good family! You have heard the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>. You need not wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) ever again. Nor will birth, old age, and death exist for them again. Then separation from what is cherished and union with what is unpleasant will not occur. You will go, O son of good family, to the world-system of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss). You will hear the <s>Dharma</s> in the presence of <s>Amitābha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Thus, O son of good family, those beings will have a happy death. Then <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, departed to one side. Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> remained in silence. And the gods, <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial beings), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), humans, and non-humans departed.

Then <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'How do I know, Blessed One, that the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, brings about complete liberation from all sins?' The Blessed One said: 'There exists, O son of good family, on the southern side of <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, two sacred fords — one pure and one impure — established by seven Perfectly Enlightened Ones. Now they have been fashioned by me. Just as a white cloth takes on a dark hue, so should that heap of sins be regarded. Even so, O son of good family, this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, burns all sins and produces a state of perfect purity. Just as, <s>Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin</s>, during the rainy season all grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees become verdant in appearance, and then a <s>Nāgarāja</s> (serpent king) named <s>Śatamukha</s> (Hundred-Faced), descending from his abode, burns all those grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees — even so, O son of good family, this <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, burns all sins and produces a state of purity. Happy will those beings be who

children.text: yadā te prakrāntāstadāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavānasmākaṃ śikṣāsaṃvaram / bhagavānāha - ye bhikṣava upasaṃpadābhāvamicchanti, taiḥ prathamataraṃ gatvā āvāsaṃ samyagavalokayitavyam / vyavalokayitvā bhikṣuka(?)mārocayitavyaṃ śuddhayate bhadanta nānāvāsaṃ na ca yatra nānāvāse 'sthīni saṃvidyante / uccāraprastāve na saṃvidyete / pariśuddhayati / evaṃ bhadanta nānāvāsamarhati upasaṃpadābhāvo bhikṣūṇām //
children.translated_text: When they had departed, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach us the training precepts.' The Blessed One said: 'Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) who desire the state of full ordination should first go and properly examine the dwelling place. Having examined it, they should report to the <s>bhikṣu</s>: "The dwelling place is pure, venerable sir — there is no communal dwelling, and in the communal dwelling there are no bones to be found. There are no latrines nearby. It is purified." Thus, venerable sir, a communal dwelling is fit for the full ordination of <s>bhikṣus</s>.'

children.text: bhagavānāha - duḥśīlena bhikṣuṇā nopasaṃpādayitavyam / na ca jñaptirdātavyā / kiṃ bahunā? bhikṣavo duḥśīlena bhikṣuṇā nānāvāsaṃ na kartavyam, prāgeva jñapticaturtham / ete hi śāsanadūṣakāḥ / duḥśīlānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ śīlavatāṃ dakṣiṇīyāṇāṃ madhye āvāso na dātavyaḥ / teṣāṃ bahirvihāre āvāso dātavyaḥ / tathā saṃghālāpo na dātavyaḥ / na ca teṣāṃ sāṃghikī bhūmimarhati / na ca teṣāṃ kiṃcidbhikṣubhāvaṃ saṃvidyate //
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'An immoral <s>bhikṣu</s> should not perform ordination, nor should a formal motion be given. In short, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, an immoral <s>bhikṣu</s> should not establish a communal dwelling — much less perform a fourfold formal act. These are corrupters of the teaching. An immoral <s>bhikṣu</s> should not be given a dwelling among virtuous, worthy <s>bhikṣus</s>. They should be given a dwelling outside the monastery. Likewise, a share of the communal provisions should not be given to them. Nor do they deserve the communal grounds. Nor does any state of being a <s>bhikṣu</s> exist for them.'

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - katame kāle bhagavannīdṛśādakṣiṇīyā bhaviṣyanti? bhagavānāha - tṛtīye varṣaśatagate mama parinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya īdṛśādakṣiṇīyā bhaviṣyanti, ye vihāre gṛhisaṃjñāṃ dhārayiṣyanti / te dārakadārikāparivṛtā bhaviṣyanti / te sāṃghikaṃ mañcapīṭhaṃ vaṃśikopabimbopadhānakaṃ śayanāsanaṃ asatparibhogena paribhokṣyante / ye ca sāṃghikopacāre uccāraṃ prasrāvaṃ kurvanti, te vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryāmuccāraprasrāve gūḍhamṛttikodare prāṇino jāyante / ye sāṃghikaṃ dantakāṣṭhamasatparibhogena paribhuñjante, te kūrmamakaramatsyeṣu jāyante / ye sāṃghikaṃ tilataṇḍulakodravakulatthadhānyādīnasatparibhogena paribhūñjante, te pretanagareṣupapadyante / hīnendriyā dagdhasthūṇākṛtibhirasthipatravaducchritaiḥ svakeśaromapraticchannaiḥ parvatodarasaṃnibhaiḥ sūcīchidropamamukhaiḥ kāye īdṛśaṃ te duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavanti / ye sāṃghikasyānnapānāderanyāyena paribhogaṃ kurvanti, te 'lpaśruteṣu kuleṣu jāyante / hīnendriyāśca jāyante / khañjakubjakāṇavāmanāśca jāyante / paramukhayācanakāśca jāyante / tataścottari vyādhitāśca jāyante / pūyaśoṇitaṃ kāye vahanti / svakīyalomasaṃkucitakāyā uttiṣṭhanti, tadā māṃsapiṇḍā bhūmau patanti / asthīni dṛaśyante / evaṃ te bahūni varṣaśatāni kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavanti / ye sāṃghikīṃ bhūmimasatparibhogena paribhuñjante, te dvādaśa kalpān raurave mahānarake upapadyante / teṣāṃ taptānyayomuhāni mukhe (
Vaidya 308
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 308]

children.text: ) viṣkambhānte dahyante / oṣṭhamapi, dantā api viśīryante / tālūni sphūṭanti dahyante / kaṇṭhamapi tālvapi hṛdayamapi / anyānyapi sarveṇa sarvaṃ dahyante, avaśeṣaṃ gacchanti / tadā bhikṣavaḥ karmavāyavo vānti yena te mṛtāḥ purūṣāḥ punareva jīvanti / tataḥ punarapi yamapālaiḥ puruṣaiḥ saṃgṛhyante / tataḥ teṣāṃ karmopagānāṃ karmavaśānāṃ mahatī jihvā prādurbhavati / tatra jihvāyāmupari halaśatasahasraṃ kṛṣyate / evaṃ te bahūni varṣaśatāni bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi bahūni varṣaśatasahasrāṇi nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavanti / tataścyutvā agnighaṭe mahānarake upapatsyante / tataste yamapālapuruṣā gṛhītvā ca tasya jihvāyāṃ sūcīśatasahasraṃ vidhyanti / tadapi karmavaśājjīvanti, tata utkṣipya agnikhadāmadhye kṣipanti / tasyāmagnikhadāyāmutkṣipya mahatīṃ vaitaraṇīṃ kṣipanti, tadapi kālaṃ na kurvanti, tadanyanarakeṣupapadyante / evaṃ parikramatāṃ teṣāṃ trayaḥ kalpāḥ parīkṣīyante / tataścyutvā jambūdvīpe jāyante daridrāḥ jātyandhāḥ / tasmātte hyanindānyuttarāṇi sāṃghikāni vastūni rakṣitavyāni //
children.translated_text: are burned to the very end. The lips also, the teeth also crack apart. The palates burst and burn. The throat, the palate, and the heart also — all other parts are entirely burned and consumed. Then, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), the winds of <s>karma</s> blow, by which those dead men come to life again. Then once more they are seized by <s>Yama's</s> attendants.

Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'At what time, O Blessed One, will there be such unworthy recipients of offerings?' The Blessed One said: 'Three hundred years after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), there will be such unworthy recipients who will maintain the perception of householders while in the monastery. They will be surrounded by boys and girls. They will use the communal beds, seats, and bamboo furnishings of the <s>Saṃgha</s>,

children.text: ye bhikṣavaḥ śikṣāsaṃvarasaṃvṛtāśca bhavanti, taiḥ imāni trīṇi cīvarāṇi dhārayitavyāni / ekaṃ cīvaraṃ saṃghasya viśvāsena saṃghaparibhogāya, tathā dvitīyaṃ cīvaraṃ rājakuladvāragamanāya ca, tṛtīyaṃ cīvaraṃ grāmanagaranigamapallīpattaneṣu ca / imāni trīṇi cīvarāṇi bhikṣavo dhārayitavyāni / ye śīlavanto guaṇavantaḥ prajñāvantastairbhikṣava imāni śikṣāpadāni mayā prajñaptāni dhārayitavyāni / asatparibhogena bhikṣavo na paribhoktavyaṃ sāṃghikaṃ vastu agnighaṭopamam / sāṃghikaṃ vastu viṣopamam / sāṃghikaṃ vastu vajropamam / sāṃghikaṃ vastu bhāropamam / viṣasya pratīkāraṃ kartuṃ śakyate, na tu sāṃghikasya vastunaḥ pratikāraṃ kartuṃ śakyate //
children.translated_text: Those <s>bhikṣus</s> who are restrained by the discipline of training should wear these three robes: one robe for the use and benefit of the <s>Saṃgha</s> (monastic community) entrusted to it, a second robe for going to the gates of royal palaces, and a third robe for visiting villages, towns, market-towns, hamlets, and trading posts. These three robes, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should be worn. Those who are virtuous,

children.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - ājñaptāni bhagavatā śikṣāpadāni, ye bhikṣavo dhārayanti, te pratimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛtā bhavanti / vināyābhimukhā bhavanti / kośābhimukhā bhavanti / śikṣākuśalā bhavanti / tāni ca bhagavataḥ śikṣāpadāni bhavanti //
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'The training rules have been proclaimed by the Blessed One. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> who uphold them are restrained by the discipline of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code). They are devoted to the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic rules). They are devoted to the <s>Kośa</s> (treasury of teachings). They are skilled in the training. These are the training rules of the Blessed One.'

children.text: āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā prakrāntaḥ / atha te mahāśrāvakāḥ svakaṃ svakaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ prakrāntāḥ / te ca devā nāgā yakṣā gandharvā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragā manuṣyāḥ, sarve te prakrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, departed. Then those great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) departed each to their own <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field). And those <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and humans — all of them departed.

children.text: iti śikṣāsaṃvaro nāma dvādaśaṃ(?) prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth(?) chapter, called 'The Discipline of Training.'

children.text: idamavocadbhagavān, te ca bodhisattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti //
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, that entire assembly, and the whole world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

children.text: ayaṃ kāraṇḍavyūhamahāyānasūtraratnarājasya dhāraṇivyūhaḥ maheśvaraḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: This concludes the <s>Dhāraṇīvyūha</s> <s>Maheśvara</s> section of the <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>.

children.text: āryakāraṇḍavyūho mahāyānasūtraratnarājaḥ samāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: The noble <s>Kāraṇḍavyūha</s>, the king of jewels among <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s>, is completed.

children.text: ye dharma hetuprabhavā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from a cause — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus has spoken the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s> (Ascetic).
